additional.en:
Completion methods

There will be lectures, online lecture notes, study groups, and exercises, or some subcombination of these and possibly other forms of teaching.

Some activity during the course (e.g. in the form of gathering enough exercise points and attending study groups) is required to attend the course exam.

A separate exam can be taken with independent study and does not require attendance.

The course may be arranged in a different format and with different assessment methods for open university students.

Assessment practices and criteria

The grading scale is 0...5. Half of the available course points is required for the lowest passing grade of 1 and 5/6 of the points is required for the highest grade 5 with linear scaling for the other grades.

Points are awarded for the exam and for completing exercises with most of the points coming from the exam. The course may also involve study groups with mandatory attendance but no points for grading.

The course can also be taken with a separate exam with no participation to the exercises or study groups.

Deviations from the scheme are possible depending on the difficulty of the exam.

Activities and teaching methods in support of learning

There will be online lecture material, which is sufficient for independent study. Weekly lectures present the core material with additional explanation and examples.

Students are given exercise problems which require the knowledge and skills described in the learning outcomes. In weekly exercise meetings students present their solutions to the problems and discuss them with a teacher. Model solutions to the problems are provided online to support independent study.

In study groups students read research articles or other material where the core techniques of the course are utilized in an advanced way. During the study group meetings the students discuss the reading material and explain it to other students.

Target groups
Optional course in a compulsory module for all students of the Programme. Belongs to the Discrete Algorithms study module. Available also to students from other degree programmes. Suitable for exchange students (if prerequisites met).

content.en:
The Internet of Things (IoT) is an extension of Internet connectivity into everyday objects and physical devices. Modern IoT devices integrate many sensors which provide measurements characterising the device, its environment, or its user. These data are emerging as one of the fastest growing areas for data science.

The Data Science for the Internet of Things course covers the fundamentals of developing data science processing pipelines for data produced by Internet of Things devices. The course covers all common phases within data science pipelines: data collection, ground truth collection, feature engineering, and data modelling and evaluation.

The content of the course includes:

· Introduction to the Internet of Things, pervasive computing, data science

· Sensing and signal processing

· Pipelines and programming of Data science for the Internet of Things

· Privacy and security for Data Science for the Internet of Things

· Challenges and opportunities of Data Science for the Internet of Things Systems.

additional.en:
Completion methods

The course will be offered in contact teaching. Grading is based on final exam and weekly exercises.

Assessment practices and criteria

The grading scale is 1- 5 (weekly exercises 50%, final exam: 50%).

Students must complete at least 50% of the weekly exercises and 50% of the final exam to pass the course.

Attending the lectures and exercise session is not mandatory, but participation can be considered to improve the final grade.

Activities and teaching methods in support of learning

The teaching methods are updated from year to year.

Moodle is the main platform used during the course. The weekly lectures focus on developing the week's topic. The lecture materials will be online after each session. The weekly exercises are developed according to the week's topic and serve as evaluators of problem-solving.

The weekly study groups focus on solving the submitted exercises and summarizing the weekly lectures.

Target groups

The course is intended for Master and Doctoral students. The course is also available to students from different degree programmes. Exchange students are welcomed.

Recommended time/stage of studies for completion

The course is suggested to be taken after completion of at least one of the recommended prerequisites courses and at any time during the Master or Doctoral studies.

Term/teaching period when the course will be offered

Yearly during Spring term (period 4)

Study module

The course is part of the Master's Programme in Computer Science (Networks study track) and the Master's Programme in Data Science, an optional course for advanced studies.

tweetText.fi: Learn how to build data warehouses and perform business intelligence analysis in the era of Big Data
tweetText.sv: Learn how to build data warehouses and perform business intelligence analysis in the era of Big Data

outcomes.en:
After the course, the student will

  • Understand the limits with OLTP databases
  • Can explain the four characteristics of data warehouses
  • Know the main components of a data warehouse
  • Understand ETL phases and their main issues
  • Can compare different terms including standard DB, data warehousing, OLTP, heterogeneous databases
  • Understand the star schema, snowflake schema, fact constellations
  • Can formulate OLAP operations: drilling, rolling, slicing, dicing, and pivoting
  • Understand MOLAP, ROLAP, and HOLAP
  • Can write OLAP queries in SQL
  • Understand Business intelligence (BI) and its application
  • Understand independent and dependent data marts
  • Understand the difference between Inmon versus Kimball approaches for data warehousing
  • Understand Lambda and Kappa big data architectures
  • Know the main products for data warehousing and BI
  • Understand the difference between a real-time data warehouse and a traditional data warehouse
  • Know the difference between ACID and BASE
  • Understand various data models and operations, including relational, semi-structured, graph data models
  • Know the four NoSQL databases: Key-value, document, wide-column, and graph databases
  • Understand the difference between tightly integrated polystores, loosely integrated polystores, and hybrid polystores
  • Understand GFS, HDFS and YARN
  • Can design efficient MapReduce models to solve computing problems

Students learn about data warehouse and business intelligence as a possible career and as a path towards deep expertise in the data warehouse. Students learn also group work and interaction skills during exercise sessions.

additional.en:
Completion methods

There will be lectures, study groups, and exercises. There is no final exam (renewal exam or separate exam) for this course. Students are required to attend this course and complete all exercises to pass the course. This course can be arranged in a different format and with different assessment methods for open university students

Assessment practices and criteria

The course's activities include study groups and exercises (including hands-on problems). A total of 100 points can be earned from the course's activities.

Activities and teaching methods in support of learning

Lectures: Attending lectures is not obligatory but it is useful. Lecture notes covering key facts will be posted on this page, but there will be additional examples and explanations during the lectures. We will also explain the answers to questions in self-assessment forms in lectures.

Exercises: The students should solve the problems at home and be prepared to present their solutions at the exercise session. The students are required to solve ALL problems. Give yourself as much time as possible to complete each assignment so you can complete it to the best of your ability and you don't have to rush or worry about incurring late submission penalties. The exercises will include several hands-on problems with data warehouse software.

Study groups: The students read some material in advance and then discuss the material in groups during the meeting. Attending the study group meetings is mandatory. But if you have a reason (such as an emergency, personal illness, or others) for being absent, please let the lecturer know before the meeting.

Target group

The course is not offered every year. It is offered every two years, alternatively in Spring.

First or second spring of studies

Advanced studies in computer science; Software study track

outcomes.en:
After completing the course, the student should be able to: 

 • Describe the fundamental elements of relational database management systems 

• Explain the basic concepts of the relational data model, entity-relationship model, relational database design, relational algebra

 • Can write SQLs to retrieve desired data for relational database • Design ER-models to represent simple database application scenarios 

• Understand the normal-form theory (1NF,2NF,3NF, BCNF) and improve the database design by normalization. 

• Familiar with basic database storage structures and access techniques: file and page organizations, indexing methods including B tree, and B+ tree 

• Understand the ACID properties of transaction and recoverability and serializability schedule 

• Gain hand-on experience with PostgreSQL database

outcomes.en: Students will be able to recognize the problems of processing data of large scale that arise in engineering and computer science. The focus is in statistical inference, learning and optimization methods for large scale data.  Students will know the basic theory of such problems, concentrating on results that are useful in computation. Students will have a thorough understanding of how such problems are thought of and addressed, and some experience in solving them. Students are expected to be able to apply the methods of large scale data analysis in their own research work. They will know a number of examples of successful application of the large scale data analysis techniques in different areas. More detailed and revised learning outcomes are presented at the beginning of the course.

name.fi: Scalable Systems and Data Management D
name.sv: Scalable Systems and Data Management D

outcomes.en:
After completing the course, students will be able to

  • Define the requirements, building blocks, and challenges when architecting, building and managing a large-scale data-center infrastructure for distributed systems and databases.
  • Know the design principles and implement code for engineering scalable data-intensive systems and their applications; analyze the full system stack for managing and scheduling data-center resources in relation to distributed storage, coordination and computation.
  • Critically assess the trade-offs between different requirements when designing scalable distributed systems; Understand the trade-offs in converting between data models and database tools.
  • Understand new data models and new storage technologies, as well as their impacts on query execution, database systems, cloud platforms, data processing pipeline, and modern machine learning systems.        
  • Discuss, compare and criticize the state-of-the-art research approaches presented in research papers targeting distributed systems, databases and machine learning systems.

prerequisites.en: Recommended prerequisites: Students should either (1) complete the follow courses at Aalto: CS-C3140 Operating Systems, CS-A1155 Databases for Data Science, CS-C3150 Software Engineering, CS-E4110 Concurrent Programming, CS-E4190 Cloud Software and Systems or (2) demonstrate the understanding of concepts and technologies in operating systems, databases, networks, distributed systems, software engineering and virtualization and container techniques. Furthermore, students must program well with at least two programming languages in C++, C, Java, Rust, Python and Go. content.en: This course is on the design and implementation of scalable data management systems. Topics include data-center technologies, data models (relational, document, key/value), storage models, query languages, storage architectures, indexing, query processing and optimization, in-memory databases, distributed storage, distributed coordination (consensus protocols and use-cases), transaction processing and concurrency control, new storage media, and parallel architectures (multicores/multi-socket/chiplet), as well as studies on open-source/commercial distributed database systems to illustrate these techniques and trade-offs.

additional.en:
Target group

Master's Programme in Computer Science is responsible for the course

  • CSM14000 - Software Systems study track
  • Data Management  course package CSM14300
  • Module in Data Management CSM24300

The course is available to students from other degree programmes (this seminar can be available to students with Master of Data Science)


Timing

Recommended time for completion is spring the first or second year of the Masters programme.

The seminar is in Spring term and will be offered every year.


Completion methods
The grading will be based on each student's own written work (1/3), oral presentation (1/3), and commentary as an opponent on the presentations and reports of others as well as activeness in general (1/3). To pass the seminar, each of these components must be passed. (Active) attendance of seminar meetings is obligatory. Absence from at most two meetings is accepted (and will affect grading).
Recommended optional studies

To continue with a Master's thesis in computer science related to the topic of the seminar.

Academic writing courses


Contents

We are in the era of “big data”. Data sets grow fast in size because they are increasingly being gathered by cheap and numerous information-sensing mobile devices, remote sensing, software logs, cameras, microphones, and wireless sensor networks. Most big data environments go beyond relational databases and traditional data warehouse platforms. The increasing focus on collecting and analyzing big data is shaping new platforms and techniques. This seminar will mainly discuss new research papers in different subfields of big data management, including data querying, exploration, sampling, sharing, cleansing, big data benchmark and applications.


Activities and teaching methods in support of learning

Teacher's lectures and students' presentations and reports.


Assessment practices and criteria

Students complete this seminar by actively participating in its work: the work methods include studying scientific sources, writing reports and giving presentations, reading the reports of other participants and evaluating them.


Keywords

Suitable for exchange students

learningMaterial.en:
1. Hadoop and Spark platforms (Volume, Velocity, Variety)

(1) Juwei Shi, Jia Zou, Jiaheng Lu, Zhao Cao, Shiqiang Li, Chen Wang: MRTuner: A Toolkit to Enable Holistic
Optimization for MapReduce Jobs. PVLDB 7(13): 1319-1330 (2014)

(2) Juwei Shi, Yunjie Qiu, Umar Farooq Minhas, Limei Jiao, Chen Wang, Berthold Reinwald, Fatma Özcan:
Clash of the Titans: MapReduce vs. Spark for Large Scale Data Analytics. PVLDB 8(13): 2110-2121
(2015)

(3) Yuxing Chen, Jiaheng Lu, Chen Chen, Mohammad Hoque, Sasu Tarkoma: Cost-effective Resource Provisioning for Spark Workloads. CIKM 2019: 2477-2480


2. Cloud data management (Volume, Velocity)


(1) Yaser Mansouri, Adel Nadjaran Toosi, Rajkumar Buyya: Data Storage Management in Cloud Environments: Taxonomy, Survey, and Future Directions. ACM Comput. Surv. 50(6): 91:1-91:51 (2018)

(2) Yue Wang, Alexandra Meliou, Gerome Miklau: Lifting the Haze off the Cloud: A Consumer-Centric Market for Database Computation in the Cloud. PVLDB 10(4): 373-384 (2016)

(3) Adam Silberstein, Russell Sears, Wenchao Zhou, Brian F. Cooper: A batch of PNUTS: experiences connecting cloud batch and serving systems. SIGMOD Conference 2011: 1101-1112

(4) Vaidas Gasiunas,et al: Fiber-based architecture for NFV cloud databases. PVLDB 10(12): 1682-1693
(2017)

3. Data sampling (Volume, Velocity)


(1) Ying Yan, Liang Jeff Chen, Zheng Zhang: Error-bounded Sampling for Analytics on Big Sparse Data. PVLDB  7(13): 1508-1519 (2014)

outcomes.en:
After completing the course, the participants will be able to:

(1) describe problems, tasks, and methods related to data management in machine learning,

(2) mention specific works in the literature related to the topic of the course and explain how they contribute to the field,

(3) discuss the validity and merit of technical contributions in the field,

(4) suggest ideas for further research in the field.

content.en:
In this seminar, participants will read, present, and discuss research articles and book chapters on topics related to data management tasks that arise in standard machine learning (ML) settings, such as data acquisition, data quality, sampling and coresets, in-DB machine learning, efficient inference, and end-to-end ML optimizations.

The seminar is based on a preselected set of research articles and book chapters that will serve as the primary material of the course, along with suggestions for background and additional reading.

additional.en:
Completion methods

The course is completed via participation in teaching.

Assessment criteria

* Successful completion of the course requires participation in the lectures, responsiveness in the discussions, timely return of the deliverables, and professional conduct.

* The teacher assesses and gives the final grade, in a scale 0-5. However, the student also provides a self-assessment of the deliverables.

* The assessment criteria for the deliverables include: (1) the extent to which the deliverables address the questions and requested tasks in their description; (2) the accuracy and depth of the delivered content, (3) the quality of language and presentation. An assessment matrix will be provided during the course.

Activities and methods in support of learning

The course contains lectures, video presentations by the participants on works from the literature, in-person and online discussion, and writing of a literture review.

Target groups

The main target groups are students from the Computer Science (CSM) and Data Science (DATA) programs at the University of Helsinki.

Teaching period when the course will be offered

Periods III-IV.

Recommended time or stage of studies for completion

The recommended time for completion is during the second year of studies in the CSM or DATA programs.

However, students who have already completed the prerequisite courses are welcome to attend the seminar during their first year of studies.

Language of instruction

English

tweetText.en: Explore the cutting-edge advancements in multi-model databases in the age of AI.

outcomes.en:
After the course, a student:

• Demonstrate the ability to design and implement data schemas that leverage multiple data models in a single database.

• Develop proficiency in writing queries across different data models using appropriate query languages

• Explore various AI techniques that can be integrated with multi-model databases to enhance data retrieval and analysis.

• Apply data analytics techniques to extract insights from complex datasets stored in multimodel databases.

• Investigate case studies where multi-model databases and AI technologies are applied in industries such as finance, healthcare, and e-commerce.

content.en:
This pilot course consists of the attendance of a minimum number of "ELLIS Distinguished lectures" or talks of similar nature, picked from a list we compile from seminars and presentations organized by the CS research labs. The students will need to complete a written assignment for each lecture to deepen and showcase their understanding. The class is aimed towards all students within CS and this is reflected in both the selected lectures and the assignment.

Attending ELLIS lectures, or others from visiting researchers, and completing related assignments will provide a unique opportunity to see the application of knowledge and expertise obtained during their studies. It will also expose the students to state-of-the-art research from various topics in CS, enabling them to 'dip their toes' in different potential future (research) directions.

name.en: Capstone: Data Science for Business II D
name.fi: Capstone: Data Science for Business II D

outcomes.en: The course introduces modern methods in predictive modelling (e.g. quantile/convex regression and deep learning) and provides an introduction to Explanable Artificial Intelligence (xAI) and Interpretable Machine Learning (IML). Upon completion of the course, students will be able to apply machine learning techniques to support business decision making.
outcomes.fi: The course introduces modern methods in predictive modelling (e.g. quantile/convex regression and deep learning) and provides an introduction to Explanable Artificial Intelligence (xAI) and Interpretable Machine Learning (IML). Upon completion of the course, students will be able to apply machine learning techniques to support business decision making.

prerequisites.en: Recommended prerequisites: Data Science for Business I; Business Analytics 1 or 2 or equivalent skills. Intermediate / advanced skills in Python or R programming. Intermediate understanding of multivariate calculus is assumed (e.g. Mathematical tools for analytics).
prerequisites.fi: Recommended prerequisites: Data Science for Business I; Business Analytics 1 or 2 or equivalent skills. Intermediate / advanced skills in Python or R programming. Intermediate understanding of multivariate calculus is assumed (e.g. Mathematical tools for analytics).

content.en:
The content may vary from year to year depending on the lecturers. A more detailed description of the actual content for the implementation will be provided in the course syllabus on MyCourses before registration for the implementation opens.

The examples of topics are:
- Advanced regression techniques (quantile/convex regression)
- Image recognition using convolutional neural networks (CNN)
- Text analysis and NLP using recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and transformers
- Introduction to Explainable Artificial Intelligence (xAI) and Interpretable Machine Learning (IML)

The course consists of pre-recorded lecture videos and tutorials in Python for the topics. Python assignments and theory tests will be used to assess student knowledge.

The course is intended for BIZ students. Therefore, in addition to the theoretical foundations, the applications (not the development) of the methods will be presented. Lectures are designed to provide the in-depth material, while the assignments are designed to try out the methods.
Knowledge of Python is assumed, but the tutorials are detailed and the assignments are designed considering that coding is a secondary skill.

outcomes.en:
The objective of the course is to provide an introduction to practical data science from the perspective of business
analysts. Part of the course material touches also more advanced topics to provide further content for the students that are interested in knowing more about the underlying theory and techical aspects.

After completing the course, students will understand the basic principles of predictive modeling and gain experience in using machine learning models to solve business problems.

name.fi: Advanced Topics in Software Systems D
name.sv: Advanced Topics in Software Systems D

outcomes.en:
This course focuses on advanced topics in software systems. The topics will be centered around software systems techniques for edge-cloud continum, distributed and end-to-end machine learning, and new continuum computing models, such as cloud-hpc-quantum integration.  The study is centered around researching new ideas, evaluating existing techniques, optimizing systems and exploring new solutions. Students will be able to:

  • classify and explain state of the art of systems requirements for big data and ML in edge-cloud continuum
  • analyze and apply key metrics and system designs of Big Data/ML applications and services
  • define and develop reliability and performance monitoring and analysis of systems for big data and ML
  • apply and evaluate key programming models and frameworks for Big Data/ML
  • produce and evaluate edge system designs for Big Data and ML systems
  • present and discuss new hardware architectures and quantum for Big Data/ML
  • present and discuss future perspectives on systems for Big Data/ML

outcomes.en:
Upon completing the bachelor’s thesis, the student is able to

1. investigate a scientific or engineering topic in their area of interest and report the results of the investigation in written thesis form and in an oral presentation;

2. express the goals of the investigation as well-defined scientific or technical questions;

3. work systematically from an initially modest knowledge of the topic area toward an in-depth understanding;

4. find scientific literature relevant to the topic, read it analytically and critically, and identify its contributions and significance to their own work;

5. organise and analyse information from the literature, producing a clearly scoped, carefully argued, and well-presented synthesis and conclusions, answering the posed questions;

6. attribute information to its source following good scientific practices;

7. work independently and systematically, take expert advice, and participate constructively in a peer group;

8. abide by the standards of academic integrity and research ethics.
outcomes.fi:
Kandidaatintyön kirjoitettuaan opiskelija osaa

1. tutkia tieteellistä tai teknistä aihetta oman mielenkiintonsa alueelta ja raportoida tutkimuksen tulokset kirjallisen opinnäytteen muodossa sekä suullisessa esityksessä;

2. ilmaista tutkimuksen tavoitteet hyvin määriteltyinä tieteellisinä tai teknisinä kysymyksinä;

3. edetä järjestelmällisesti aihepiirin vähäisestä tuntemuksesta kohti sen syvällistä ymmärtämistä;

4. löytää aiheeseen liittyvää tutkimuskirjallisuutta, lukea sitä analyyttisesti ja kriittisesti sekä tunnistaa sen kontribuutiot ja merkityksen oman työnsä kannalta;

5. organisoida ja analysoida kirjallisuuden tietoa selkeästi rajatuksi, huolellisesti argumentoiduksi ja hyvin esitetyksi synteesiksi ja johtopäätöksiksi, jotka vastaavat asetettuihin kysymyksiin;

6. viitata tiedon lähteisiin noudattaen tieteellisen kirjoittamisen käytäntöjä;

7. työskennellä itsenäisesti ja järjestelmällisesti, ottaa vastaan asiantuntijan ohjausta, ja työskennellä rakentavasti vertaisryhmässä;

8. noudattaa akateemisen yhteisön eettisiä sääntöjä.
outcomes.sv:
Efter att ha slutfört kandidatarbetet kan studeranden

1. undersöka ett vetenskapligt eller tekniskt ämne inom sitt intresseområde och redovisa resultatet av undersökningen i form av ett skriftligt examensarbete och en muntlig presentation;

2. uttrycka undersökningens mål som väldefinierade vetenskapliga eller tekniska frågor;

3. arbeta systematiskt från en begränsad kunskap om ämnesområdet mot en fördjupad förståelse;

4. hitta vetenskaplig litteratur som är relevant för ämnet, läsa den analytiskt och kritiskt och identifiera dess bidrag och dess betydelse för sitt eget arbete;

5. organisera och analysera information från litteraturen, producera en tydligt avgränsad, noggrant argumenterad och väl presenterad syntes och slutsatser, och därmed svara på de ställda frågorna;

6. hänvisa till informationskällor enligt god vetenskaplig praxis;

7. arbeta självständigt och systematiskt, ta emot handledning av en expert och delta konstruktivt i en grupp av likar;

8. följa normerna för akademisk integritet och forskningsetik.

name.fi: Special Course in Machine Learning, Data Science and Artificial Intelligence D: Simulation based inference

outcomes.fi: At the end of this course, you will be familiar with the sub-field of simulation-based inference (SBI), and the various methods that fall under this umbrella, such as approximate Bayesian computation, neural posterior estimation and neural likelihood estimation. You will be able to implement some of them popular SBI methods on simple examples, learn about some of the Monte Carlo techniques used in SBI, and become familiar with and present the state-of-the-art research in the field.

prerequisites.fi: Linear algebra, Bayesian data analysis or equivalent knowledge in Bayesian analysis, familiarity with probability and statistics, deep learning

content.fi: In this course, we will look at a family of approximate Bayesian inference methods specialized for scientific models that do not have a tractable likelihood function, called simulation-based inference (SBI) methods. In the past couple of decades, SBI has become a real driving force in data-driven sciences and technology, where model parameters are notoriously difficult to estimate but simulating data from the model is straightforward. We will learn about the various types of SBI methods in the literature, namely, approximate Bayesian computation, neural posterior and likelihood estimation, among others, and how to implement them in practice. We will also discuss some of the primary challenges faced by contemporary SBI methods, and the recent works on tackling them.

outcomes.en: After the course, the students will have a general understanding of data, data usage, data ethics, and the benefits of data in business activities. The students will also have a clear understanding of what contemporary strategic data management requires, and why leading with data can accrue better business results. Students will also have an idea of possible situational factors affecting leading with data, and the potential challenges and risks that may happen when leading with data in different business contexts. Furthermore, the course will include an introduction to different analytical tools which can help in data management and reporting, in other words, how data can be presented (visualized), how it can be interpreted, and used in decision-making processes in business contexts.

Opiskelijoille syntyy myös ymmärrys siitä, minkälaisiin organisatorisiin tilanteisiin tiedolla johtaminen ei välttämättä sovi ja mitkä ovat tiedolla johtamisen mahdolliset haasteet ja riskit eri liiketoimintakonteksteissa. Osaa soveltaa eettisiä näkökohtia tietojenkäsittelyyn.

Tieto- ja viestintätekniikan historiaa ja ajankohtaisia ilmiöitä, kuten tekoäly, esineiden internet, big data.

outcomes.en:
After the course, a student:

Can identify and explain central societal implications of computing. For this, the student has to a sufficient extent made acquaintance with the history of the field and current phenomena. Can identify and describe some central risks related to privacy, security and sustainability. Can identify and describe some approaches and methods for controlling the risks.

Can describe the essence of computer science and its position among other areas of research.

Can explain what computer ethics and professional societal responsibility are about. Can identify some of the field’s central professional and other organizations. Can describe the importance of codes of ethics and list main points of at least two major codes of ethics.

Can identify and explain some central principles related to copyright, software licenses and software patents. Can describe what the philosophy of open sources software is about and can identify some licenses for open source software. Can list some central rights for individuals ensured by the data protection regulation and requirements for computing professionals posed by the regulation.

The course gives training in especially the following academic expert skills: ethical thinking, development of thinking about sustainability, responsibility and the future, andsystems thinking.

Osaa kuvailla tietojenkäsittelytieteen olemusta ja sen asemaa muiden tieteenalojen joukossa.

content.en:
History and current phenomena in information and communication technology (ICT), such as artificial intelligence, internet of things, big data.

Definition of computer science and its position among other areas of research.

Professional and scientific organizations in the field of computing; standardization bodies.

Information society: computing and democracy, social media, freedom of search, digital divide, accessibility.

Computing and sustainability.

Privacy and security: philosophical basis for privacy and security, risks such as privacy violations, computer crime and vulnerability of the information society, requirements for computing professionals posed by the data protection regulation, pseudonymization and anonymization of data collections.

Intellectual property rights as well as free and open source software and open data: philosophical basis for intellectual property rights, copyright, software patents and software licenses, trademarks and trade secrets, open data, free and open source software.

outcomes.fi:
Kurssin jälkeen osaat

  • kuvailla tietokoneen perusrakenteen ja kertoa mitä tapahtuu koneen käynnistyksessä
  • kertoa missä kaikkialla tietokone voi säilyttää tietoa
  • kertoa mikä on prosessi ja mikä sen merkitys on ohjelman suorituksessa
  • selvittää verkkonumeron ja verkkonimen yhteyden sekä muuntaa verkkonumeron sitä vastaavaan binäärimuotoon ja toisinpäin
  • kuvailla Internetin rakenteen ja sen keskeiset toimintaperiaatteet
  • laatia konekielisen ohjelman, joka käsittelee yksinkertaista tietorakennetta ja arvojen sijoittamista muuttujille
  • selittää ja kuvata erilaisia tiedonesitystapoja sekä tehdä lukumuunnoksia erilaisten lukujärjestelmien välillä
  • selittää usean prosessin suorittamista ja keskeytysten käsittelyä
  • kuvata verkkoviestien lähettämisen ja vastaanottamisen
  • selittää Internetin keskeiset palvelut ja protokollat (DNS, HTTP, TCP, IP, DHCP, reititys) ja niiden toiminnan
  • perustella tiedon suojauksen merkityksen ja selittää jonkun esitellyn menetelmän toiminnan periaatteet.

Kurssi harjaannuttaa erityisesti seuraavissa yleisissä akateemisista asiantuntijataidoissa: ryhmätyö, ammattikirjallisuuden lukeminen suomeksi ja englanniksi, akateeminen kirjoittaminen, ajanhallinta sekä rakentavan vuorovaikutuksen taidot.

Kurssi harjaannuttaa myös alan yleisiä taitoja kuten komentotulkin ja LaTeXin peruskäyttöä.

outcomes.en: In this course you will learn how to use the computer effectively as a working tool. You will learn how to use Linux from the command line, handle large files, manage projects with the Git version control system, and write technical reports with LaTeX.
outcomes.fi: Tällä kurssilla opit käyttämään tietokonetta tehokkaasti työvälineenä. Opit käyttämään Linuxia komentoriviltä, käsittelemään isojakin tiedostoja, hallitsemaan projekteja Git-versionhallintajärjestelmällä, ja kirjoittamaan teknisiä raportteja LaTeX-ladontajärjestelmällä.
outcomes.sv: I den här kursen får du lära dig att använda datorn effektivt som arbetsredskap. Du får lära dig att använda Linux från kommandoraden, hantera stora filer, hantera projekt med versionskontrollsystemet Git och skriva tekniska rapporter med LaTeX.

content.en:
The course consists of four modules:

  1. Linux: command line efficiency, automating routine tasks with shell scripts.
  2. Git: using the version control system to manage projects, also in a team.
  3. LaTeX: technical and mathematical writing with LaTeX.
  4. Data: efficient handling of large files.
content.fi:
Kurssi koostuu neljästä moduulista:

  1. Linux: komentorivin tehokäyttö, rutiinitehtävien automatisointi shell-skripteillä.
  2. Git: versionhallintajärjestelmän käyttö projektien hallitsemiseen myös työryhmässä.
  3. LaTeX: tekninen ja matemaattinen kirjoittaminen LaTeX-ladontajärjestelmällä.
  4. Data: isojenkin tiedostojen tehokas käsittely.
content.sv:
Kursen består av fyra moduler:

  1. Linux: effektiv användning av kommandoraden, automatisering av rutinuppgifter med skalskript.
  2. Git: använda versionskontrollsystemet för att hantera projekt, även i team.
  3. LaTeX: tekniskt och matematiskt skrivande med LaTeX.
  4. Data: effektiv hantering av stora filer.

outcomes.en:
After this course the student 

  • can explain "how internet works" and justify the architectures, technical and functional principles used in internet. These include network entities, functional models, addresses and identifiers, data transfer in protocol model, reliable data transfer, flow control, congestion control.
  • can explain network application models client-server and peer-to-peer, as well as the principles used in the implementation phase od network application.
  • Can explain what is name service (DNS), what is it used for and its structure and functionalities 
  • Can explain how the packets are send and delivered from the sender to the receiver. Also how they are processed at the sending and receiving nodes.
  • Can explain what are routers, switchers, hubs and repeaters, how they work, including their similarities and differences.
  • can explain packets, frames and other message structures, contents and usages in several different protocols.
  • know and can describe main risks and security threads related to networking, can explain what is firewall and how it works.
outcomes.fi:
Opintojakson suoritettuaan opiskelija

  • osaa selittää ”miten Internet toimii” ja perustellen kuvata siinä käytettyjä rakenteellisia, teknisiä ja toiminnallisia periaatteita (kuten toimintamallit, rakenneosat, erilaiset osoitteet ja tunnisteet, datan siirto protokollapinon avulla, luotettava kuljetuspalvelu, vuonvalvonta, TCP:n ruuhkanhallinta).
  • osaa selittää asiakas-palvelija malliin perustuvien verkkosovellusten sekä niiden toteutuksessa käytettyjen sovellusprotokollien periaatteet. Osaa kuvata vertaistoimijamallin idean. Osaa selittää, mihin tarvitaan nimipalvelua (DNS) ja kuvata sen rakenteen ja toiminnan.
  • osaa selittää toisaalta miten lähettävän ohjelman viesti saadaan IP-pakettiin ja toisaalta miten IP-paketti välitetään Internetissä viestin vastaanottajalle.
  • osaa selittää reitittimen, keskittimen ja kytkimen toiminnan ja erot. Osaa kuvata pakettien, kehysten ja muiden viestien sisältöjä ja rakenteita.
  • osaa kuvata tietoliikenteeseen kohdistuvat riskitekijät ja turvallisuusuhat. Osaa selittää kuinka palomuuri toimii.

outcomes.en: After completing this course,, the student knows different software intended for numerical analysis, knows different ways of presenting and storing data, understands the basic principles of computing, e.g. its limitations and knows how to analyze and visualize datasets with different software. The focus of the course is the automation of solutions by means of algorithmic thinking (as a series of well-defined steps), the identification, analysis, comparison and implementation of different solution options with the aim of finding an effective solution, as well as generalizing and transferring the problem-solving process to a wide range of similar computational problems.
outcomes.fi: Kurssin käytyään opiskelija tietää erilaisia numeeriseen laskentaan tarkoitettuja ohjelmistoja, tuntee erilaisia tiedon esitys- ja tallennustapoja, käsittää laskennan perusperiaatteet ml. sen rajoitteet ja osaa analysoida ja visualisoida tietoaineistoja erilaisilla ohjelmistoilla. Kurssin keskiössä on ratkaisujen automatisointi algoritmisen ajattelun keinoin (sarjana hyvin määriteltyjä askeleita), erilaisten ratkaisuvaihtoehtojen identifiointi, analysointi, vertailu ja implementointi (toteutus) tavoitteena löytää tehokas ratkaisu, sekä yleistää ja siirtää ongelmanratkaisuprosessi laajaan joukkoon samankaltaisia laskennallisia ongelmia.
outcomes.sv: Efter genomgången kurs kan studenten olika programvaror avsedda för numerisk analys, kan olika sätt att presentera och lagra data, förstår de grundläggande principerna för datoranvändning, t.ex. dess begränsningar och vet hur man analyserar och visualiserar dataset med olika programvaror. Fokus för kursen är automatisering av lösningar med hjälp av algoritmiskt tänkande (som en serie väldefinierade steg), identifiering, analys, jämförelse och implementering av olika lösningsalternativ med syfte att hitta en effektiv lösning, samt generalisera och överföra problemlösningsprocessen till ett brett spektrum av liknande beräkningsproblem.

content.en: Through practical exercises, the course introduces the processing and visualization of research data using various programming, domain-spesific, and mark up languages ​​and software such as Python, SQL, MATLAB, Simulink, and HTML5. The goal is to know how to organize information logically and formulate computational problems in such a way that it is possible to solve them using the methods typically used in Computer Science and to process, present and analyze information at different levels of abstraction such as models and simulations.
content.fi: Kurssilla tutustutaan käytännön harjoitustöiden kautta tutkimusdatan käsittelyyn ja visualisointiin erilaisilla ohjelmointi-, täsmä-, ja merkintäkielillä sekä ohjelmistoilla, kuten Python, SQL, MATLAB, Simulink ja HTML5. Tavoitteena on osata organisoida tietoa loogisesti ja muotoilla laskennallisia ongelmia siten, että ne on mahdollista ratkaista tietojenkäsittelytieteiden keinoin sekä tuottaa, esittää ja analysoida tietoa eri abstraktiotasoilla kuten malleina ja simulaatioina.
content.sv: Genom praktiska övningar introducerar kursen bearbetning och visualisering av forskningsdata med hjälp av olika programmerings-, domänspecifika och uppmärkningsspråk och mjukvara som Python, SQL, MATLAB, Simulink och HTML5. Målet är att veta hur man organiserar information logiskt och formulerar beräkningsproblem på ett sådant sätt att det är möjligt att lösa dem med de metoder som vanligtvis används inom datavetenskap och att bearbeta, presentera och analysera information på olika abstraktionsnivåer såsom modeller och simuleringar.

content.en:
In future an electronics designer must have an understanding of a hardware-software interface and of restrictions a hardware can cause for softwares. Also a design methodology requires a good basic knowledge in programming, as programming is widely utilized in electronics design. On the course one becomes acquainted with a design process of an electronic device in a way, where modelling, simulation and finally controlling and operating system are connected to be one programmatic ensemble.

On the course a student develops his/her programming skills in a way which promotes hardware design and the course familiarizes the student with the powerful prorgammatic methods from an electronics design perspective. The course familiarizes the student with typical designing environments and different stages of the programmatic harware design from the modelling to the implementation are went through. The course provides to students an excellent starting point to improve their know-how in programming and in hardware design in their further studies.
content.fi:
Tulevaisuuden elektroniikkasuunnittelijan on ymmärrettävä laitteisto-ohjelmistorajapinta ja laitteiston ohjelmistoille aiheuttamat rajoitukset. Myös suunnittelumetodiikka edellyttää hyvää ohjelmoinnin perusosaamista, sillä elektroniikkasuunnittelusssa hyödynnetään laajasti ohjelmointia. Kurssissa tutustutaan elektronisen laitteen suunnitteluprosessiin siten, että laitteiston mallintaminen, simulointi ja lopulta ohjaus- sekä käyttöliittymä  yhdistetään yhdeksi ohjelmalliseksi kokonaisuuudeksi.

Kurssilla opiskelijan ohjelmointitaitoja kehitetään laitteistosuunnittelua tukevaan suuntaan ja hänet tutustutetaan tehokkaisiin ohjelmistollisiiin työtapoihin elektroniikkasuunnittelun näkökulmasta. Kurssilla perehdytään tyypillisiin ohjelmallisiin suunnitteluympäristöihin ja käydään läpi ohjelmallisen laitteistosuunnittelun eri vaiheet mallintamisesta toteutukseen. Kurssi tarjoaa opiskelijalle erinomaisen lähtökohdan kehitttää ohjelmointi- ja laitteistosuunnitteluosaamistaan eteepäin myöhemmissä opintojen vaiheissa.
content.sv:
Framtidens planerare inom elektronik måste förstå gränssnitten för hårdvara och programvara samt de begräsningar som hårdvaran uppställer för programvaror. Även planeringsmetodiken förutsätter bra grundkunskaper i programmering eftersom man utnyttjar dessa kunskaper omfattande i planeringen inom elektronik. På kursen bekantar man sig med planeringsprocessen av en elektronisk apparat så att apparaturens modellering, simulering och slutligen styr- och operativsystem sammanfogas till en helhet.

På kursen utvecklar studenten sina kunskaper i programmering till en riktning som stöder planeringen av apparaturer. Studenten bekantar sig även med effektiva arbetssätt ur elektronikplaneringens synvinkel. På kursen sätter man sig in i typiska omgivningar för planeringen av programvaror och genomgår olika faser i planeringen av apparaturer från modelleringen till förverkligandet. Kursen erbjuder en utmärkt utgångspunkt åt studenten att utveckla sin kompetens i programmering och planering av apparaturer vidare i senare skeden av studierna.

content.en: This course introduces and applies dynamic heterogeneous agent models to study policy questions related to taxation, social insurance, and pension systems. The models considered include the neoclassical growth model with wealth and labour income heterogeneity as well as life cycle and overlapping generations models of labour supply and savings with uninsurable income risks. For each model, we also discuss issues related to numerical methods and calibration.

additional.en:
Completion methods (general description)

The course consists of lectures (24 hours) and exercise sessions (8 hours), where solutions to the homework assignments are discussed. The lectures and exercise sessions are not mandatory.

There is a written final exam based on the lecture material and the homework assignments. The homework assignments consist of analytical and numerical exercises. They familiarise the student with the theory and calculations typically required in applying and extending the models that have been studied in the lecture. They also involve the interpretation of model economies.


Assessment practices and criteria

The grade on a scale from 0 (fail) to 5 is based on the points earned in the final exam (70%) and in the homework assignments (30%).


Learning activities and methods

The course material is delivered through the course website. The website also contains moderated discussion groups that support learning. Homework assignments/problem sets are designed to support learning of the course material.

Master’s Programme in Economics (Research track). Open also to doctoral students in economics.

name.en: Applications of quantum physics I: atoms and molecules
name.fi: Applications of quantum physics: atoms and molecules
name.sv: Applications of quantum physics I: atoms and molecules

outcomes.fi: Student is able to understand the basics of quantum physics, especially the concepts and basic principles of wave mechanics. Understands how and under what circumstances quantum mechanics and classical mechanics merge to one another. Understands how quantum mechanics can be dealt with in three dimensions in the simplest physical situations such as the hydrogen atom. Knows the concepts and distributions of statistical mechanics and understands where they come from, and is able to utilize them in the analysis of quantum mechanical distributions. Is able to understand how one can move on from atoms towards molecules.

prerequisites.fi: It is assumed that the students participating in the course have previously completed the course BSPH2004 (basics of quantum physics) or acquired the corresponding background information.

content.fi: A brief discussion of the background of quantum mechanics as an introduction to the course. The connection between quantum mechanics and classical mechanics. Wave mechanics in three dimensions: Radial equation and its solutions in the case of Coulomb's potential. Electron wave functions of hydrogen atom, spectrum of hydrogen atom. Multi-electron wave function and symmetry properties of identical particles. Atomic electron orbital structure, periodic system. The basics of statistical mechanics and its key distributions, as well as the differences between classical and quantum mechanical distributions. Time permitting, the atom in the magnetic field and the Zeeman phenomenon.

additional.fi:
Completion methods

The course is partly completed by returning answers to exercises that will be assessed, and by a course exam, or alternatively by an exam. Exercises are not obligatory, but the activity in calculating exercises has a positive effect on the grade.

Grading scale is 0 (failed) - 1 (passed) - 5 (excellent)

Weekly lectures, independent work by the student, weekly exercise sessions, which are partly done in calculation workshops in small groups, and partly independently.

name.fi: Applications of quantum physics: solid state and elementary particles

tweetText.fi: Introduction to the building blocks of matter at different scales, their properties and interactions

outcomes.fi:
After this course, you will have acquired a knowledge of the basics of modern solid state, nuclear, and particle physics. In particular, you should be able to:

  • Describe the building blocks of matter and their interactions at different scales, starting from elementary particles via atomic nuclei and atoms to crystal structures and special states of matter (superfluidity, BEC, superconductivity)

  • Compare and contrast the properties of conductors, insulators, and semiconductors and explain their differences by the band structure

  • Recall basic relations in nucleus models in order to explain fission/fusion and their relation to binding energies

  • Predict activity by application of the nuclear decay law

  • Apply conservation laws to ascertain the possibility of particle decays

  • Analyze a set of experimental data and prepare a project summary in scientifically

    appropriate style.

prerequisites.fi: From the Bachelor's Programme in Science curriculum: Basic studies in physics, Introduction to quantum physics, and Applications of quantum physics I.

content.fi:
Solid state physics: crystal structures, Bragg scattering, conductors, insulators, semiconductors, definitions of para, dia, and ferromagnetism.

Superconductors and superfluids: energy gap and superfluidity, Bose-Einstein condensates, Meissner effect, Josephson junction.

Structure of nuclei: masses and binding energies, the droplet and shell model, strong interaction.

Nuclear reactions: radioactivity, exponential decay law, fission, and fusion.

Basics of elementary particles: leptons, baryons, mesons. New quantum numbers and conservation laws: the quark model, quantum chromodynamics, standard model of particle physics.

outcomes.en:
After completing this course, students should have acquired the following skills:
- Basic understanding of core public-key cryptographic primitives, e.g. public-key encryption, signatures, commitments, and argument systems.
- How to construct core public-key cryptographic primitives over algebraic structures.
- How to reason about the security of constructions based on the conjectured hardness of computational problems over algebraic structures.
- How to securely compose core public-key cryptographic primitives to build advanced primitives, e.g. advanced encryption schemes, privacy-preserving signature schemes, protocols for computational tasks with privacy guarantees.
- Familiarity of security and privacy goals achievable via cryptographic techniques in realistic privacy-preserving applications.

content.en:
This is an intermediate-level course on cryptography, with focus on public-key, application-oriented cryptographic primitives. It covers definitions and constructions of core and advanced public-key primitives, and their applications in privacy-preserving systems.

In particular, we cover the following core primitives:
- Public-key encryption
- Signatures
- Commitments
- Zero-knowledge arguments

content.en: The course provides an introduction to the methods of modern applied macroeconometrics. The main emphasis is on the vector autoregressive (VAR) model, but other approaches employed in applied work are also briefly reviewed, and their relation to the structural VAR model is discussed. In particular, we concentrate on the identification of economic shocks by various methods and the use of the structural vector autoregressive framework in empirical research and policy analysis. Classical statistical inference in reduced-form and structural VAR models as well as tools of structural analysis are covered. The course starts with a review of the reduced-form VAR model, followed by tools of structural analysis in the VAR framework, including the impulse response function, forecast error variance decomposition, historical decomposition and counterfactual analysis. The identification of structural VAR models by short- and long-run identification restrictions as well as identification using statistical properties of the data is next covered. The structural VAR approach is contrasted with alternatives, including DSGE and dynamic simultaneous equations models. The emphasis is on practical application of the methods discussed in modelling macroeconomic and other data. Although various alternative approaches put forth in the previous economic literature are briefly reviewed, in this course, we concentrate on the linear VAR model, which is the most widely employed framework in applied research and policy work.

additional.en:
Completion methods (general description)

The course consists of lectures (24 hours) and exercises either in separate sessions or integrated into the lectures. The lectures (and exercise sessions) are not mandatory.

There is a written final exam, a number of the homework assignments, and an empirical term paper. The homework assignments consist of analytical and empirical exercises. The former familiarise the student with the theory and calculations typically required in the practical implementation of the methods, while the latter teach skills of undertaking an empirical research project, including data handling, programming and interpreting results.

Assessment practices and criteria

The grade on a scale from 0 (fail) to 5 is the weighted average of the grades of the final exam (50%), the homework assignments (25%), and the term paper (25%). Each of the three components is graded on a scale from 0 (fail) to 5, and each must be passed separately.

Learning activities and methods

All material related to the course is delivered through the Moodle area of the course, which also contains a discussion forum where students can discuss issues related to the course with each other and the teacher. Homework assignments and the term paper are submitted through the Moodle area of the course.

Target groups

Students of the Master’s Programme in Economics (General Track and Research Track). Open to students of other degree programmes and study tracks and exchange students. The course can also be part of the continuous learning offerings of the degree programme.

Teaching period when the course will be offered

At least every other year in the fourth period

Recommended time or stage of studies for completion

First spring term

Study modules
ECOM-G300, ECOM-R300, ECOM-Y300
Languages of instruction

English

EQF level
Master's/EQF level 7

content.en:
The goal of the course is to provide an introduction to the methods of modern applied, quantitative macroeconomics. The course builds on existing dynamic stochastic (general) equilibrium models. The aim is to learn to solve numerically macroeconomic models for which closed-form solutions are not available. We will focus on both the basics of global solution algorithms and solution algorithms of linear rational expectation models. We will calibrate the model parameters and evaluate the quantitative performance of the models compared with empirical observations.

Students apply the learned methods, i.e. implementing and solving macroeconomic models, in a series of coding exercises. At the end of the course, the students submit a term paper and codes on a final project where they attempt a (partial) replication of a paper of their own choice from the literature. The project may include a calibration exercise, a policy experiment, or a computational exercise.

outcomes.en:
After the course:

  • The student masters the basic definitions and terminology relevant for X-ray scattering and can make use of these in real experimental work, for example when estimating optimum experimental conditions for an X-ray scattering experiment.
  • The student can judge which materials properties can be studied using X-ray scattering methods.
  • The student is familiar with the common X-ray scattering methods and can distinguish which X-ray scattering method is appropriate for a specified materials characterization task.
  • The student can plan an X-ray scattering experiment to be carried out together with technical support.
  • The student can carry out X-ray scattering experiments using an X-ray scattering instrument at Aalto.
  • The student can report the results of an X-ray scattering experiment in a scientific article and critically judge the results published by others.

content.en:
Plasma is the fourth and most common state of matter in our cosmos. Our direct contacts with plasma are still -- fortunately -- few and far apart. However, since e.g., modern tele communication is based on basic properties of plasmas, and fusion energy could help slow down the climate change, learning some basics of this peculiar state of matter is not only interesting but also useful.
In this course the student will be introduced to plasma, a gas consisting of electrically charged particles, which makes its properties dramatically different from those of the more familiar states of matter: the free charges interact via Coulomb force that has, in principle, infinite range. This allows plasma to display a host of interesting collective phenomena, the most useful and intriguing of which  will be introduced in this course. The plasma will be treated predominantly with the magnetohydrodynamic description, the foundations of which will be outlined.

  • Design and deliver a group presentation based on a collaboratively written scientific report.

name.en: Quantum physics applications - Atoms and molecules

outcomes.en: Please see the course description for the course BSPH2005
outcomes.fi: Osaa kvanttifysiikan perusteet ymmärtäen etenkin aaltomekaniikan käsitteet ja perusperiaatteet. Ymmärtää kuinka ja missä olosuhteissa kvanttimekaniikka ja klassinen mekaniikka yhtyvät toisiinsa. Ymmärtää kuinka kvanttimekaniikkaa voi käsitellä kolmessa ulottuvuudessa yksinkertaisimmissa fysikaalisissa tilanteissa kuten vetyatomin tapauksessa. Osaa statistisen mekaniikan käsitteet ja jakaumat ja ymmärtää mistä ne tulevat, sekä pystyy hyödyntämään niitä myös kvanttimekaanisten jakaumien tarkastelussa. Pystyy näkemään kuinka atomeista siirrytään edelleen kohti molekyylejä.
outcomes.sv: Att känna till grunderna i kvantfysik och förstå hur strukturen hos atomer och molekyler uppstår som en följd av kvantmekaniken och vågfunktioner . Att förstå de diskreta energinivåerna hos atomer och molekyler, hur dessa kan exciteras elektroniskt, rotationellt och vibrationellt, samt hur olika yttre omständigheter såsom magnetfält kan påverka dessa. Att känna till olika typer av bindningar mellan atomer och molekyler.

prerequisites.en: Please see the course description for the course BSPH2005
prerequisites.fi: Oletuksena on, että kurssille osallistujat ovat aikaisemmin suorittaneet opintojakson FYS2003 Kvanttifysiikan perusteet tai hankkineet vastaavat taustatiedot.
prerequisites.sv: Det förutsätts att kursdeltagareär bekanta med innehållet i kursen FYS2003 Kvantfysikens grunder.

content.en: Please see the course description for the course BSPH2005
content.fi: Lyhyt kvanttimekaniikan taustan keskustelu johdantona opintojaksoon. Kvanttimekaniikan ja klassisen mekaniikan välinen kytkentä. Aaltomekaniikkaa kolmessa ulottuvuudessa: Radiaaliyhtälö ja sen ratkaisut Coulombin potentiaalin tapauksessa. Vetyatomin elektronin aaltofunktiot, vetyatomin spektri. Monielektroniaaltofunktio ja identtisten hiukkasten symmetriaominaisuudet. Atomien elektroniverhon rakenne, jaksollinen järjestelmä. Statistisen mekaniikan perusteet ja sen keskeiset jakaumat sekä klassisten ja kvanttimekaanisten jakaumien erot. Ajan salliessa myös atomi magneettikentässä ja Zeemanin ilmiö.
content.sv: Lösning av den radiella vågfunktionen för atomer med en elektron och applicering på väteatomen. Väteatomens energinivåer och urvalsregler för elektroniska övergångar. Elektronens spinn och atomers växelverkningar med magnetfält, Zeemann-effekten. Atomer med flera elektroner, centralfältsmodellen. Symmetriska och antisymmetriska vågfunktioner. Molekyler och bindingar mellan atomer: kovalenta, jonbindingar, Van der Waals, vätebindningar. Rotationer och vibrationer i molekyler. Elektroniska övergångar i molekyler.

additional.en: Please see the course description for the course BSPH2005
additional.fi:
Suoritustavat

Kurssi suoritetaan osittain arvosteltavaksi palautettavilla laskuharjoituksilla ja kurssikokeella tai vaihtoehtoisesti tentillä. Laskuharjoitukset eivät ole pakollisia, mutta aktiivisuus laskuharjoituksissa vaikuttaa positiivisesti arvosanaan.


Arviointimenetelmät ja -kriteerit

Arvosteluasteikko 0-5. Arvosanan määräytyminen (Koulutusohjelman parhaat käytänteet, Wiki).


Oppimista tukevat aktiviteetit ja opetusmenetelmät

Viikottaiset luennot, opiskelijan itsenäinen työskentely, viikoittain palautettavat laskuharjoitukset, joita lasketaan osittain laskupajoissa assistenttien tuella pienryhmissä ja osittain itsenäisesti. Laskuharjoitukset palautetaan assistenteille, jotka pisteyttävät ne.


Kohderyhmät

Fysikaalisten tieteiden kandiohjelman opiskelijat ja muiden koulutusohjelmien opiskelijat.


Järjestämisajankohta opetusperiodin tarkkuudella

Opintojakso järjestetään vuosittain syyslukukaudella 1. periodissa. Opintojaksoa ei poikkeuksellisesti järjestetä lukuvuonna 2023-2024.


Suositeltava suoritusajankohta tai -vaihe

Suositeltu suoritusajankohta fysikaalisten tieteiden kandiohjelmassa: 3. opiskeluvuosi, periodi I. Katso tarkemmat opintosuuntakohtaiset ohjeet opintojen ajoitusmalleista.


Opintokokonaisuus

Opintojakso kuuluu pakollisena fysiikan (FYS2100) ja fysiikan laaja-alaisen kandin (FYS2200) aineopintokokonaisuuksiin. Muilla fysikaalisten tieteiden opintosuunnilla opintojakson voi sisällyttää valinnaisiin aineopintoihin. Muiden koulutusohjelmien opiskelijat voivat sisällyttää opintojakson fysikaalisten tieteiden opintokokonaisuuksiin (FYS1901 ja FYS1902) tai fysiikan aineopintokokonaisuuteen (FYS2700).

Opintojakso kuuluu pakollisena myös fysiikan aineenopettajan aineopintokokonaisuuteen MFK-F200.
additional.sv:
Prestationssätt
Kursen kan avläggas via (a) utförande av räkneövningar som returneras för granskning och slutförhör, eller (b) sluttentamen. Närvaro på föreläsningar krävs inte.


Bedömningsmetoder och kriterier

Kursens bedöms på basen av de returnerade räkneövningarna, möjliga kursarbeten och sluttentamen på skalan 0-5.


Aktiviteter och metoder som stöder lärandet

Deltagande i föreläsningar och räknesmedjor, utförande och returnering av räkneövningar och aktivitet då modellösningar presenteras stöder inlärningen.


Målgrupper

Kursen erbjuds till studerande i kandidatprogrammet i fysikaliska vetenskaper och också till studerande från andra utbildningsprogram.


När studieavsnittet ordnas – undervisningsperiod

Studieavsnittet ordnas varje hösttermin, periodi I. Studieavnittet ordnas inte under läsåret 2023-2024.


Rekommenderad tidpunkt för prestationen

Rekommenderad tidpunkt: Tredje studieåret, period I. Se mer detaljerade instruktioner om modeller för studietid.


Studiehelhet

Studieavsnittet hör till ämnesstudier i fysik (FYS2600, obligatorisk).

name.en: Quantum physics applications - Condensed matter and elementary particles
name.fi: Kvanttifysiikan sovelluksia - Tiivis aine ja alkeishiukkaset
name.sv: Kvantfysikens tillämpningar - Det fasta tillståndet och elementarpartiklar

outcomes.en: Please see the course description for the course BSPH2006
outcomes.fi: Opiskelija tuntee kvanttifysiikan tärkeimmät modernit sovellukset: johteet, eristeet ja puolijohteet; suprajohteet ja -nesteet; atomiytimien rakenteen; ydinreaktiot; alkeishiukkasten perusteet. Ymmärtää kuinka ja missä olosuhteissa kvanttimekaniikka ja klassinen mekaniikka yhtyvät toisiinsa. Osaa kvalitatiivisesti selittää tärkeimmät ilmiöt kuten elektroniaukot ja johdevyöt, Fermi-pinta, PN-liitos, Meissnerin efekti, Bose-Einstein kondensaatio, BCS teoria. Osaa käsitellä kvantitatiivisesti puolijohtavuutta, ytimien sidosenergioita, radioaktiivista hajoamislakia sekä ydin- ja hiukkasreaktioita.
outcomes.sv:
Lära sig:

  • kristallstrukturer, gitter och millerindex, samt grunderna för röntgendiffraktion
  • elektronstrukturen och olika modeller för att beskriva den
  • de viktigaste koncepten inom kvantfysiken, såsom ledare, halvledare, isolatorer och supraledare
  • atomkärnans egenskaper och olika modeller för kärnan
  • radioaktivitet och kärnreaktioner
  • standardmodeller samt partiklar och konserveringslagarna
  • grunderna för Feynmandiagram, kvantfältteorin och modeller utöver standardmodellen
  • acceleratorer och hur de kan användas inom partikelfysiken

FYS2003 Kvantfysikens grunder och FYS2005 Kvantfysikens tillämpningar - Atomer och molekyler

content.en: Please see the course description for the course BSPH2006
content.fi:
Kiinteän olomuodon fysiikka: hilarakenne, Braggin sironta, johteet, eristeet, puolijohteet sekä magnetismi.
Suprajohteet ja nesteet: energia-aukko ja suprajuoksevuus, Bose-Einstein-kondensaatti, Meissnerin ilmiö, Josephson-liitos.
Atomiytimien rakenne: massat ja sidosenergiat, pisara- ja kuorimalli, vahva nukleoni-nukleoni-vuorovaikutus.
Ydinreaktiot: radioaktiivisuus, eksponentiaalinen hajoamislaki, fissio ja fuusio.
Alkeishiukkasten perusteet: leptonit, baryonit, mesonit; uudet kvanttiluvut ja säilymislait; kvarkkimalli, kvanttiväridynamiikka ja hiukkasfysiikan standardimalli.
content.sv:
Fasta tillståndets fysik: kristallstrukturer, gitter, millerindex, röntgendiffraktion, ledare, halvledare, isolatorer och supraledare

Atomkärnan och kärnprocesser: atomkärnan, kärnmodeller, radioaktivitet och kärnreaktioner

Partikelfysik: standardmodellen, partiklar, konserveringslagar, teoretiska stukturen, modeller utöver standardmodellen och acceleratorer

Yksinkertaisten matriisimallien rakentaminen niin, että ne jäljittelevät maailman ilmiöitä likimääräisesti. Laskennallisesti tehokkaiden ratkaisumenetelmien suunnittelu ja kirjoittaminen Matlabilla.

content.fi:
Matemaattinen mallinnus. Matriisilaskuun perustuvien ratkaisujen muokkaaminen algoritmimuotoon Matlabilla.

Matriisilasku on sovelletun matematiikan keskeisin työkalu. Käytännön sovelluksissa matriisilasku ja lineaarialgebra näyttäytyvät aina algoritmien muodossa, ja siksi tällä kurssilla harjoitellaan matemaattista ohjelmoimista. Ohjelmointikielenä toimii juuri tähän tarkoitukseen kehitetty Matlab.

Kurssilla perehdytään lineaarialgebran ja matriisilaskennan käyttöön tietokoneohjelmoinnin keinoin. Kurssilla toteutetaan mallinnusalgoritmeja käytännön ongelmiin, kuten valokuvien käsittelyyn, virtuaalisen tilan valaistuksen laskentaan, vaahteranlehtien muotojen Prokrustes-analyysiin ja numeeriseen integrointiin. Kurssin esimerkkien sisältö vaihtelee hiukan vuosittain, mutta matemaattiset tekniikat ovat samat.

Tehtäviä ei ole pakko tehdä etukäteen, vaan ne voi toteuttaa harjoituksissa. On myös mahdollista palauttaa ratkaisut sähköpostitse, eli etäsuorittaminen on täysin OK.

Luennoitsija opettaa livekoodauksen keinoin. Luentojen ruutukaappausvideoita sekä muutakin oppimateriaalia julkaistaan YouTubessa ja UniTubessa.

outcomes.en:
After taking the course, the student is able to

  • carry out demanding physical measurements according to instructions
  • use different measuring devices
  • apply the theory of physics to practice
  • scientifically analyze the measurement results and to present them as tables and graphs
  • write a clear and consistent measurement report following the laboratory work.
outcomes.fi:
Opintojakson suoritettuaan opiskelija

1. osaa tehdä kokeellisen fysiikan mittauksia ohjeistuksen mukaan,
2. osaa käyttää erilaisia mittalaitteita,
3. osaa soveltaa fysiikan teoriaa käytäntöön,
4. osaa käsitellä mittaustuloksia tieteellisellä tavalla ja esittää niitä taulukkoina ja graafeina,

  • utföra krävande fysiska mätningar enligt instruktioner

  • tillämpa teorin om fysik för fysiska mätningar
  • analysera mätresultaten vetenskapligt och presentera dem som tabeller och diagram

content.en: In this course, the students will familiarize themselves with various physical phenomena by making measurements and analyzing the obtained results. The course consists of both experimental and computational laboratory projects whose topics support and complement the 2nd year lecture courses in physics.
content.fi: Kurssilla tutustutaan fysiikan ilmiömaailmaan itse tehtyjen mittausten ja saatujen tulosten analysoinnin avulla. Kurssiin kuuluu sekä kokeellisia että laskennallisia laboratoriotöitä, joiden aiheet tukevat ja täydentävät teknillisen fysiikan pääaineen 2. vuoden luentokursseja.
content.sv: Kursens målsättning är att bekanta deltagarna med fysikens fenomen med hjälp av mätningar och analysering av mätningsresultat. Kursen består av både experimentella och beräkningsmässiga laboratoriearbeten som stödar och kompletterar fysikkurser i 2. årskursen.

outcomes.fi: Kurssin suoritettuaan opiskelija osaa kertoa miksi kvanttimekaniikkaa tarvitaan ja tuntee kvanttimekaniikan teoreettiset perusteet. Opiskelija osaa käsitellä kaksitilasysteemiä ja muodostaa usean kaksitilasysteemin tensoritulon. Opiskelija osaa kvanttimekaniikan aikakehityksen yleiset ominaisuudet ja tunnistaa Schrödingerin yhtälön. Opiskelija tuntee kvanttimekaniikan muotoilun aaltomekaniikan termein ja osaa ratkaista yksiulotteisia potentiaaliongelmia. Opiskelija osaa soveltaa kvanttimekaniikan todennököisyystulkintaa vetyatomin elektronia kuvaaviin kvanttimekaanisiin ratkaisuihin ja tuntee orbitaalin käsitteen.
outcomes.sv: Att få en inblick i kvantfenomen och veta vilka system som endast kan förstås med hjälp av kvantmekanik. Att förstå utvecklingen av kvantfysiken och dess formalism. Att kunna lösa Schrödingerekvationen för enkla fysikaliska problem.

content.fi: Kvanttimekaniikan perusteet kaksitilasysteemin avulla: tilavektorit, operaattorit, mittauksen rooli ja todenäköisyystulkinta. Kvanttimekaaninen aikakehitys ja Schrödingerin yhtälö. Aaltomekaniikkaa yhdessä ulottuvuudessa: paloittain jatkuvat kuoppa- ja porraspotentiaalit. Vetyatomin elektronia kuvaavat kolmiulotteisen Schrödingerin yhtälön ratkaisut.
content.sv:
Kvantfysikens historia.

Fotonen: svartkroppsstrålning, fotoelektriska effekten, Compton-effekten.

Atomen: atommodeller och dess kvantstruktur, Bohrmodellen.

Materievågor: våg-partikeldualitet, elektrondiffraktion, vågor och vågpaket, Heisenbergs osäkerhetsprincip.

Kvantmekanik: Schrödingerekvationen och dess sannolikhetstolkning, endimensionella lådan, harmoniska oscillatorn, väntevärden, barriärgenomträngning (tunnling).

Rörelsemängdsmomentets kvantisering: Schrödingerekvationen i sfäriska koordinater, klotytfunktioner

Atomer med en elektron: Kort introduktion till lösningen av energinivåerna hos väteatomen.

additional.fi:
Suoritustavat

Kurssi toteutetaan lähiopetuksena. Kurssin viikkottaisiin tapahtumiin osallistuminen on pakollista. Tarkemmat tiedot käytänteistä esitetään kurssin alussa ja kurssin verkkosivulla.

Opintojakso voidaan toteuttaa erilaisena toteutuksena osana koulutusohjelman jatkuvan oppimisen tarjontaa.


Arviointimenetelmät ja -kriteerit

Kurssi arvostellaan asteikolla 0-5. Arvosanaan vaikuttavat kurssikoe, laskuharjoitukset ja muut kurssilla käytettävät aktiviteetit. Arvosanan määräytymisperusteet ilmoitetaan kurssin alussa.


Oppimista tukevat aktiviteetit ja opetusmenetelmät
Viikottaiset luennot, opiskelijan itsenäinen työskentely, viikoittain palautettavat laskuharjoitukset, joita lasketaan osittain laskupajoissa assistenttien tuella pienryhmissä ja osittain itsenäisesti. Laskuharjoitukset palautetaan assistenteille jotka pisteyttävät ne.


Kohderyhmät

Fysikaalisten tieteiden kandiohjelman opiskelijat ja muiden koulutusohjelmien opiskelijat. Opintojakso on tarjolla Avoimen yliopiston kautta suomenkielisenä.


Järjestämisajankohta opetusperiodin tarkkuudella

Opintojakso järjestetään vuosittain kevätlukukaudella 4. periodissa.


Suositeltava suoritusajankohta tai -vaihe

Suositeltu suoritusajankohta fysikaalisten tieteiden kandiohjelmassa: 1. tai 2. opiskeluvuosi. Katso tarkemmat opintosuuntakohtaiset ohjeet opintojen ajoitusmalleista.


Opintokokonaisuus

Opintojakso kuuluu pakollisena fysiikan (FYS2100), fysiikan laaja-alaisen kandin (FYS2200), teoreettisen fysiikan (FYS2300) ja meteorologian (FYS2500) aineopintokokonaisuuksiin. Muilla fysikaalisten tieteiden opintosuunnilla opintojakson voi sisällyttää valinnaisiin aineopintoihin. Muiden koulutusohjelmien opiskelijat voivat sisällyttää opintojakson fysikaalisten tieteiden opintokokonaisuuksiin (FYS1901 ja FYS1902), teoreettisen fysiikan opintokokonaisuuksiin (FYS1501 ja FYS1502) tai fysiikan aineopintokokonaisuuteen (FYS2700).

Opintojakso kuuluu pakollisena myös fysiikan aineenopettajan aineopintokokonaisuuteen MFK-F200.

Bedömningsmetoder och kriterier

Kursens bedöms på basen av de returnerade räkneövningarna, möjliga kursarbeten och sluttentamen på skalan 0-5.


Aktiviteter och metoder som stöder lärandet

Deltagande i föreläsningar och räknesmedjor, utförande och returnering av räkneövningar och aktivitet då modellösningar presenteras stöder inlärningen.


Målgrupper

Kursen erbjuds till studerande i kandidatprogrammet i fysikaliska vetenskaper och också till studerande från andra utbildningsprogram. Kursen erbjuds på finska via Öppna Universitetet.
