outcomes.en:
The main goals of the course:

(1) understand the combinatorial and algorithmic aspects of logics over finite structures,

(2) learn the basic proof techniques of finite model theory such as the Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé game that can be used to characterize the expressive power of first-order logic and its variants,

(3) obtain basic understanding of the most important extensions of first-order logic over finite structures such as second-order logic, fixed-point logics, and infinitary logic,

(4) understand the fundamental connection between logics and computational complexity classes over finite structures, e.g., Fagin's theorem showing that the properties expressible in existential second-order logic correspond exactly to the complexity class NP.

prerequisites.en: Introduction to logic II

content.en:
The course discusses several topics related logics over finite structures (finite model theory):

-The Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé game and the pebble game of first-order logic and finite variable infinitary logic,

-finite automata, regular languages, and their connection to languages definable in monadic second-order logic,

- Turing machines, complexity classes, and the logical characterizations of the complexity classes PTIME and NP via existential second-order logic and least fixed-point logic,

- The zero-one law of first-order logic.

outcomes.fi:
• Students will have an understanding of the theoretical bases of common simulation methods used in computational biophysics and related fields in life sciences.
  • They understand the research areas where these methods can be used, they mainly understand how simulation methods can be integrated into experimental research and experimental data, and they are aware of the advantages and limitations of simulation methods.
  • In practice, students will have hands-on experience of doing simulations of individual biomolecules and molecular systems, to visualize the simulation data, and to analyze certain key properties of the data.
  • They will be aware of and be able to use the most common software packages employed in biomolecular simulations.

prerequisites.fi:
• Familiarity with the Linux operating system.
  • Understanding of the key principles in statistical physics / statistical mechanics, and also in classical mechanics, is recommended.
  • Understanding of computer simulation methods through more basic/intermediate courses (FYS2088 - Introduction to molecular dynamics simulations) would be useful (but not strictly compulsory).

content.fi:
• Structure, function and visualization of biological systems
  • Basics of classical molecular dynamics simulations
  • Force fields for biosimulations
  • Algorithms used in biosimulations
  • Building up simulation systems of membranes and proteins
  • Equilibration and production MD
  • Free energy calculations (umbrella sampling, thermodynamic integration)
  • Algorithms used to improve sampling (coarse graining, replica exchange, metadynamics)
  • Continuum electrostatic calculations and constant pH simulations
  • Analysis of trajectories obtained in MD simulations
  • Machine learning and Artificial intelligence techniques applied to analysis of biosimulation data
  • Quantum mechanics linked to classical biosimulations (incl. force field parameterization)

outcomes.en:
After successfully completeing this course, you will be able to:

  1. Reason about algorithms and computational problems using precise mathematical formalism and produce simple proofs.
  2. Construct a finite automaton and a context-free grammar for various natural formal languages.
  3. Describe the basic properties of regular and context-free languages and apply them for example to classify whether a given language is regular.
  4. Explain the importance of a Turing Machine in the context of undecidability, recognize typical undecidable problems, and produce simple undecidability proofs.
  5. Describe the complexity classes P, NP, NP-complete, list some central NP-complete problems, and produce simple proofs of NP-completeness.

prerequisites.en: The course Data Structures and Algorithms (or equivalent knowledge)

content.en:
The contents of the course will be updated as needed. Central topics include

  • revising basic proof techniques and other mathematical topics that are central in computer science, including basic logic and set theory.
  • regular languages, deterministic and non-deterministic finite automata, regular expressions; their applications and limitations
  • context-free languages and grammars; their applications and limitations
  • The Turing Machine and other general models of computation, the universal Turing Machine, the Church-Turing thesis
  • the concept of decidability, central results about decidability
  • polynomial time complexity; NP-completeness

additional.en:
Completion methods

The course consists of lectures, exercise sessions and examinations. The exercises can be solved independently, in small groups or in a session instructed by a teacher. Some of the exercises may involve computer programming. Attendance in exercise sessions may be compulsory if that is appropriate due to the chosen teaching method.

Alternatively, the course may be completed by taking a separate examination, in which case the written examination is the only component in passing the course.

Assessment practices and criteria

Both homework exercises and written examinations contribute to the grade. The examinations have the greatest weight, but completing a given percentage of homework may be required.

The grading scale is 1-5.

Activities and methods in support of learning

The student familiarises himself or herself to the topic by attending lectures, studying independently the textbook and other course material and finding additional material for example on the Internet. The student's understanding is deepened by solving exercises of varying form and difficulty, which is supported by guided exercise sessions.

content.en:
The course aims to provide methods and development tools to design and implement advanced torque controllers for multiphase motors configured as parallel three-phase winding sets. These multiphase topologies, typically nicknamed “multi-three-phase”, are experiencing an increasing development in transport electrification, especially in recent years. Beyond this choice, several reasons are well described in the literature and briefly summarized hereafter.

· The modularity of multi-three-phase (M3PH) drives allows the adoption of three-phase power electronics technologies, reducing costs and development time.

· An M3PH machine can be configured as multiple three-phase winding sets operating parallel and whose level of magnetic coupling among them can be designed properly according to the performance indexes of power density and short-circuit fault tolerance.

· M3PH drives implement the three-phase fault tolerance. In the case of a fault involving one three-phase unit (winding set plus inverter), this is turned off easily using several methods available in the literature (circuit breakers, PWM stop, or active short-circuit). The following advantages are thus obtained.

o Each of the remaining three-phase units operates as a balanced load, avoiding low-order harmonic content on the corresponding inverter’s dc-link.

o Each of the remaining three-phase sets produces a smooth torque without introducing a low-order harmonic ripple.

According to the above scenario, the course will present the step-by-step procedures to develop and implement high-performance torque control algorithms for M3PH permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSMs) drives, considering the cutting-edge machine typologies typically used in traction applications like PM-assisted synchronous reluctance (PM-SyR).

The course topic features several multidisciplinary aspects, including but not limited to i) dynamic modelling of M3PH PMSMs, ii) performance identification of M3PH PMSMs, and iii) design and implementation of modular torque controllers for M3PH PMSMs.

The course is highly applicative, and most of the concepts presented find direct application in the industry. This course will assume M3PH PMSMs for high-power density applications as study cases. Therefore, benchmark torque controllers for these motors will be developed and implemented.

outcomes.en: The student understands the main concepts in stochastics, mathematics and main concepts related to estimation and state estimation, the role of uncertainty in dynamic systems and is able to implement state estimation algorithms both in linear and nonlinear case. The student understands what duality between control and estimation means in control engineering and, from this point of view,  the main approaches of stochastic control.

content.en: Basics of statistics and stochastic processes. Basic concepts in estimation, ML, MAP, LS, MMSE; unbiased estimators. Linear estimation in static systems. Optimal state estimation in discrete linear dynamic systems, Kalman filter and information filter. Optimal State estimation in nonlinear dynamic systems, recursive functional relationship. Approximation of optimal nonlinear state estimation, particle filter, extended Kalman filters, 1st and 2nd order. Adaptive estimation. Duality of estimation and control. Main approaches in stochastic control.

outcomes.en:
The course provides a general introduction to the physics of polymers (basic knowledge). Structure, conformation, and properties of polymers in solution are specifically discussed. Properties of polymers in bulk are discussed in less detail. Some important experimental techniques used to study polymers are introduced as well.

Intended Learning Outcomes (ILOs): After completing course, you will be able to: Describe structural properties of key polymers and name physical parameters which influence polymer structure in solution (ILO1); Explain how the physical properties of polymers depend on their chemical properties and the properties of the solvent (ILO2); Make calculations to deduce physical parameters for polymers from experimental data (ILO3); Plan experimental research in polymer analysis (ILO4).

Exercises, an essay, an intermediate exam and the final exam. Exercises are based on homework and discussions in class. The intermediate exam is organized to help students to handle course materials.

outcomes.en: The course aims to familiarise students with theoretical findings key to both the study of politics and economics, including Arrow’s impossibility theorem, the Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem and findings pertaining to different types of voting systems. Other topics include the relationship between political decision-making and externalities, or public goods. After completing the course, students will be familiar with the basic assumptions of the topics examined and the methods of the field. Additionally, students will understand the limitations of findings and their applicability to the real world.

content.en:
This is provisional and may change especially towards the end.
1. Basics: Discrete problems, expected utility, preference notation
2. Voting methods, properties and paradoxes I
3. Voting methods, properties and paradoxes II
4. Approval voting
5. Case for strategic voting and equilibrium concept
6. Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem about manipulation of voting methods
7. Arrow’s theorem about aggregation of individual preferences into social preferences
8. Apportionment problem
9. Single peaked preferences
10. Stability of voting rules, voting about voting rule, constitutions
11. Student presentations: Solutions and failures to public goods, free riding
12. Student presentations: Solutions and failures to public goods, free riding

content.en: The goal of the course is to provide an introduction to monetary macroeconomics and the role of money and monetary policy in the economy. After describing what monetary macroeconomics is about, students will learn how the money supply is determined in the economy and how it changes. The course emphasizes price stickiness as the key factor underlying the short-run effectiveness of monetary policy. Different models are used to show how an economy can fall into a liquidity trap (zero lower bound) and what the potential measures are through which policy makers can try to lift an economy from the liquidity trap. The core of the course is optimal monetary policy. Different models also show how the time inconsistency of the optimal pre-commitment policy emerges when policy makers are dynamically optimising their policy choices and how the inflation and stabilisation bias bedevil optimal discretionary monetary policy. The aim of the course is to learn to use analytical tools to understand basic features of money and monetary policy from the point of view of the short-run macroeconomic equilibrium of an economy.

  • Microcalorimetry

outcomes.en:
The goal of the course is to develop skills in user-centric development and ability to apply these skills in product and service development.

After the course, the student

  • is familiar with key concepts and practices of product and service development and is able to apply them in practice
  • can collect and synthesize knowledge from users and other stakeholders and utilize this knowledge in product and service development
  • can evaluate and test the appropriateness of solutions in terms of needs and feasibility using prototypes
  • can communicate the progress and results of a product and service development project and is able to give and receive constructive feedback
  • can adapt oneself to work in a multidisciplinary project group and is able to analyze and develop one's own and the group's work practices
  • can describe ethical and sustainability-related aspects in product development work
outcomes.fi:
Kurssin tavoitteena on kehittää opiskelijan ymmärrystä tarve- ja käyttäjälähtöisestä kehittämisestä ja kykyä soveltaa sitä avoimien tuote- ja palvelukehityshaasteiden ratkaisemiseen.

Kurssin suoritettuaan opiskelija:

  • tuntee käyttäjälähtöisen tuote- ja palvelusuunnittelun keskeiset käsitteet ja toimintatavat sekä osaa soveltaa niitä käytäntöön
  • osaa kerätä ja koostaa tietoa ongelmakentästä käyttäjien ja muiden sidosryhmien näkökulmista sekä hyödyntää keräämäänsä tietoa kehitystyössään
  • osaa arvioida ja testata ratkaisujen toimivuutta sekä käyttäjän tarpeiden että toteutettavuuden kannalta prototyyppien avulla
  • osaa viestiä tuote- ja palvelukehitysprojektin etenemisestä ja tuloksista sekä kykenee antamaan ja vastaanottamaan rakentavaa palautetta 
  • osaa sovittautua monialaiseen projektiryhmään ja kykenee analysoimaan ja kehittämään omaa ja ryhmän toimintaa
  • hahmottaa tuotekehitystyön eettisiä ja kestävyyteen liittyviä näkökulmia
outcomes.sv:
Kursens syfte är att utveckla studentens förståelse för behovs- och användarinriktad utveckling och förmåga att tillämpa detta för att lösa öppna utmaningar inom produkt- och serviceutveckling.

Efter kursen:

  • känner studenten till de centrala begreppen och mekanismerna inom användarinriktad produkt- och tjänstedesign och kan tillämpa dem i praktiken
  • kan studenten samla och sammanställa information angående problemfältet ur användarens och övriga intressegruppers synvinkel samt nyttja informationen i sitt utvecklingsarbete
  • kan studenten utvärdera och testa lösningens funktionalitet med hjälp av prototyper, utgående både från användarens behov samt genomförbarheten.
  • kan studenten kommunicera framsteg och resultat i produkt- och serviceutvecklingsprojektet och kan ge och ta emot konstruktiv feedback
  • kan studenten anpassar sig till en multidisciplinär projektgrupp och kan analysera och utveckla sin egen och gruppens verksamhet
  • kan studenten förstå etiska perspektiv och hållbarhetsaspekter relaterade till produktutvecklingsarbete

outcomes.en:
After passing the course the student can

  1. perform physical measurements and analyze the results,
  2. explain how interference and diffraction patterns are formed,
  3. solve simple quantum mechanical systems using the Schrödinger equation,
  4. identify atomic and solid state properties based on quantum mechanics,
  5. explain the special theory of relativity and how it affects physical quantities,
  6. explain the main processes causing radioactivity.
outcomes.fi:
Kurssin suoritettuaan opiskelija osaa

  1. suorittaa fysikaalisia mittauksia ja analysoida saamiaan tuloksia,
  2. selittää valon interferenssi- ja diffraktiokuvioiden intensiteettijakauman muodostumisen,
  3. ratkaista yksinkertaisia kvanttimekaanisia systeemejä Schrödingerin yhtälön avulla,
  4. tunnistaa atomien ja kiinteän aineen ominaisuuksia pohjautuen kvanttimekaniikkaan,
  5. kertoa suppean suhteellisuusteorian perustan sekä vaikutuksen fysikaalisiin suureisiin,
  6. kuvata ydinfysiikkaan ja radioaktiivisuuteen liittyvät keskeisimmät fysikaaliset ilmiöt.
outcomes.sv:
Efter slutförd kurs kan den studerande:

  1. utföra fysikaliska mätningar och analysera resultaten,
  2. förklara hur intensitetsdistributionen för ljusets interferens- och diffraktionsmönster uppstår,
  3. lösa enkla kvantmekaniska system med hjälp av Schrödinger ekvationen,
  4. koppla ihop egenskaper hos atomer och fast materia med kvantmekaniken,
  5. förstå grunderna bakom den speciella relativitetsteorin och hur dessa inverkar på fysikaliska storheter,
  6. beskriva de centrala fysikaliska fenomenen relaterade till kärnfysik och radioaktivitet.

prerequisites.en: Recommended prerequisites: Extended mathematics curriculum in the Finnish upper secondary school, courses FY3, FY4, FY5, FY6, FY7, and FY8 (LOPS 2003) or FY3, FY4, FY5, FY6 and FY7 (LOPS 2015) from the Finnish upper secondary school when applicable and Differential and Integral Calculus 1 or equivalent.
prerequisites.fi: Suositellut esitiedot: Lukion pitkä matematiikka, lukion oppimäärän kurssi FY3, FY4, FY5, FY6, FY7 ja FY8 (LOPS 2003) tai FY3, FY4, FY5, FY6 ja FY7 (LOPS 2015) soveltuvin osin sekä Differentiaali- ja integraalilaskenta 1 tai vastaavat tiedot.
prerequisites.sv: Rekommenderade förkunskaper: Gymnasiets långa matematik, gymnasiets fördjupande kurser i fysik FY3, FY4, FY5, FY6, FY7 och FY8 (GLP 2003) eller FY3, FY4, FY5, FY6 och FY7 (GLP 2015), samt Differential- och integralkalkyl 1 eller motsvarande kunskaper.

content.en:
Always necessary material:

Knowing:  Interference and diffraction, X-ray diffraction; Schrödinger equation, probability in quantum mechanics , Heisenberg uncertainty principle, wave-particle dualism and photon; Quantum numbers, Paul s exclusion principle, periodic table of elements and spin; Solid state structure, bond types and band structure; Special theory of relativity: relativity and the speed of light; Radioactivity and decay law, nuclear reactions and binding energy.

Applying: Interference and diffraction in double slit, grid and thin film; Particle in potential well, discrete energy spectra and zero point energy; Scattering from potential wall and tunneling; Emission and absorption spectra; Conductors, semiconductors and insulators; Rest mass and relativistic energy; Fusion and fission.

Complementary material:

Knowing: Black body radiation, photoelectric effect, Compton scattering, hydrogen atom; Magnetic properties of matter; Electric conduction in metals and semiconductors; Special theory of relativity: relativity of time, place and simultaneity, relativistic energy and momentum, Lorentz-transformation; Types of radioactive radiation.

Applying: Intensity distribution in interference and diffraction patterns; Quantum mechanical oscillator; Molecular vibration spectrum; The principle of Laser; Semiconductor components; Ionizing radiation, its biological effects and protection.
content.fi:
Aina välttämätön aines:

Tietäminen: Interferenssi ja diffraktio sekä röntgendiffraktio; Schrödingerin yhtälö, kvanttimekaniikan todennäköisyysluonne, Heisenbergin epätarkkuusperiaate, aalto-hiukkas-dualismi ja fotoni; Kvanttiluvut, Paulin kieltosääntö, jaksollinen järjestelmä ja spin; Kiinteän aineen rakenne, sidostyypit ja energiavyörakenne; Suppea suhteellisuusteoria: suhteellisuusperiaate ja valon nopeus tyhjiössä; Radioaktiivisuus ja hajoamislaki, ydinreaktiot ja sidosenergia.

Soveltaminen: Interferenssi ja diffraktio kaksoisraossa, hilassa ja ohuessa kalvossa; Hiukkanen potentiaalikaivossa, diskreetti energiaspektri ja nollapiste-energia; Hiukkasen sironta potentiaalivallista ja tunneloituminen; Atomin emissio- ja absorptiospektrit; Johteet, puolijohteet ja eristeet; Hiukkasen lepomassa ja relativistinen energia; Fuusio ja fissio.

Tarpeellinen ja täydentävä aines:

Tietäminen: Mustan kappaleen säteily, valosähköinen ilmiö, Comptonin sironta, vetyatomi; Aineen magneettiset ominaisuudet; Sähkönjohtuminen metalleissa ja puolijohteissa;  Suppea suhteellisuusteoria: ajan, paikan ja samanaikaisuuden suhteellisuus, relativistinen energia ja liikemäärä sekä Lorentz-muunnos; Radioaktiivisen säteilyn eri lajit.

Soveltaminen: Interferenssi- ja diffraktiokuvion intensiteettijakauma; Kvanttimekaaninen harmoninen värähtelijä; Molekyylin värähtelyspektri; Laserin toimintaperiaate; Puolijohdekomponentit; Ionisoiva säteily, sen biologiset vaikutukset ja siltä suojautuminen.
content.sv:
Alltid nödvändigt innehåll: 

Kunskaper: Interferens, diffraktion och röntgendiffraktion; Schrödinger ekvationen, sannolikhetsbegreppet inom kvantmekaniken, Heisenbergs osäkerhetsrelation, partikel-våg dualismen och fotonen; Kvanttalen, Pauliprincipen, periodiska systemet och spin; Strukturen för fast materia, bindningar och energibandsstrukturen; Speciella relativitetsteorin: relativitetsprincipen och ljusets hastighet i vakuum; Radioaktivitet och sönderfallslagen, kärnreaktioner och bindningsenergi.

Tillämpning: Interferens och diffraktion i en dubbelspalt, i ett gitter och i ett tunt skikt; En partikel i en potentialgrop, diskreta energispektra och nollpunktsenergi; Spridning av en partikel från en potentialmur och tunnelering; Emissions- och absorptiospektra för atomer; Ledare, halvledare och isolatorer; Partikelns vilomassa och relativistiska energi; Fusion och fission.

Nödvändigt och kompletterande innehåll:

Kunskaper: Svartkroppsstrålning, fotoelektriska effekten, Compton effekten, väteatomen; Magnetiska egenskaper hos materia; Strömledning i metaller och halvledare; Den speciella relativitetsteorin: tidens, platsens och samtidighetens relativitet, relativistisk energi och rörelsemängd samt Lorentstransformationen; Olika typer av radioaktiv strålning.

Tillämpning: Intensitetsdistributionen för interferens- och diffraktionsmönster; Den kvantmekaniska harmoniska oscillatorn; Vibrationsspektret för en molekyl; Laserns funktion; Halvledartransistorn; Den joniserande strålningens biologiska effekter och strålskydd.

outcomes.en:
After the course, the student

1. knows the basics of wave propagation

2. can explain the formation of intensity distribution in interference and diffraction patterns

3. knows the Heisenberg's uncertainty principle and the wave-particle dualism in quantum mechanics

4. can solve simple quantum mechanical systems using Schrödinger's equation

5. can identify properties of atoms and condensed matter based on quantum mechanics
outcomes.fi:
Kurssin käytyään opiskelija

1. tuntee etenevän aaltoliikkeen peruskäsitteet

2. osaa selittää aaltoliikkeen interferenssi- ja diffraktiokuvioiden intensiteettijakauman muodostumisen

3. tuntee Heisenbergin epätarkkuusperiaatteen sekä kvanttimekaniikan aalto-hiukkasdualismin

4. osaa ratkaista yksinkertaisia kvanttimekaanisia systeemejä Schrödingerin yhtälön avulla

5. tunnistaa atomien ja kiinteän aineen ominaisuuksia pohjautuen kvanttimekaniikkaan
outcomes.sv:
Efter slutförd kurs

1. är du bekant med grundbegrepp kring fortskridande vågrörelse

2. kan du förklara hur intensitetsfördelningen för vågrörelsens interferens- och diffraktionsmönster uppstår

3. är du bekant med Heisenbergs osäkerhetsprincip samt kvantmekanikens våg-partikeldualitet

4. kan du lösa enkla kvantmekaniska system med hjälp av Schrödingerekvationen

5. kan du koppla ihop egenskaper hos atomer och fast materia baserat på kvantmekanik.

prerequisites.en: Recommended prerequisites: PHYS-A0110 Yliopistofysiikan perusteet, PHYS-A0130 Sähkömagnetismi, MS-A0101 Differentiaali- ja integraalilaskenta 1, or corresponding courses.
prerequisites.fi: Suositellut esitiedot: PHYS-A0110 Yliopistofysiikan perusteet, PHYS-A0130 Sähkömagnetismi, MS-A0101 Differentiaali- ja integraalilaskenta 1, tai vastaavat kurssit.
prerequisites.sv: Rekommenderade förkunskaper: PHYS-A0110 Yliopistofysiikan perusteet, PHYS-A0130 Sähkömagnetismi, MS-A0101 Differentiaali- ja integraalilaskenta 1, eller motsvarande kurser.

content.en: Interference, diffraction, dispersion, group- and phase velocity. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle, wave-particle dualism. Schrödinger's equation, statistical nature of quantum mechanics. Quantum numbers, Pauli exclusion principle, spin and periodic table of elements. Structure of solids, bond types and band structure.
content.fi: Interferenssi, diffraktio, dispersio, ryhmä- ja vaihenopeus. Heisenbergin epätarkkuusperiaate, aalto-hiukkas-dualismi. Schrödingerin yhtälö, kvanttimekaniikan todennäköisyysluonne. Kvanttiluvut, Paulin kieltosääntö, spin ja jaksollinen järjestelmä. Kiinteän aineen rakenne, sidostyypit ja energiavyörakenne.
content.sv: Interferens, diffraktion, dispersion, grupp- och fashastighet. Heisenbergs osäkerhetsprincip, våg-partikeldualitet. Schrödingerekvationen, kvantmekanikens sannolikhetskaraktär. Kvanttalen, Pauliprincipen, spinn och periodiska systemet. Strukturen för fast materia, bindningar och energibandsstrukturen.

outcomes.en:
At the end of the course the student will be able to:

Recognise the main design requirements of electrical installations in buildings

Interpret and apply related legislation, recommendations, regulations and guidelines

Recognize graphical symbols used in drawings

Make the dimensioning and sizing of electrical cables and protections

Plan and design an electrical installation

Produce and report the project drawings and descriptions

Use CAD program as a designing tool

Identifiera viktigaste planeringskrav av elinstallationer i byggnader

Igenkänna grafiska symboler använda i ritningen

outcomes.en:
• After the course the student has the basic knowledge of astronomy, space physics and space technology that are needed for further studies.
  • The student knows the structure and central physical properties of the universe and the solar system, and the objects contained in them.
  • She/he identifies the basic concepts and tools of astronomy and space physics, and is able to solve simple problems related to them.
  • The student can list what kind of observations can be made of astronomical and solar system phenomena, and what is the motivation behind such efforts.
  • She/he can compute simple orbits of satellites using celestial and orbital mechanics, and can apply various celestial coordinate systems.
  • The student recognises the basic vocabulary used in space science and technology, and how Aalto University is situated in the national and international space research scenes.

outcomes.en:
• After this course the student knows why and how information about astronomical and solar system phenomena is collected.
  • She/he can describe the physical principles on which the scientific instruments onboard satellites and probes are based.
  • The student is able to differentiate between various types of instruments and observing techniques and what they are used for, and evaluate which kind of systems are suitable for measuring certain astronomical and solar system phenomena.

outcomes.en:
At the end of the course a student is expected to be able

● Identify and discuss the requirements for the ways to sustainably utilize space for the benefit of the humankind

● Label the key challenges in sustainable utilization of space and discuss how they could be best solved now and in the future

● Hypothesize and create new ideas to promote sustainable usage of space

● Explain the basic elements of satellites and things related to their launches, and how various forms of solar activity can disturb the Earth space and create space weather effects

● Explain and discuss the legal and ethical questions that pertain to sustainable usage of space (e.g., space law, space politics, space ethics)

content.en:
● Space Sustainability MOOC is directed to all interested in space. There are no prerequisite requirements. The course is organized by the Academy of Finland Centre of Excellence in Research of Sustainable Space.

● The course provides the student with an extensive and diverse knowledge on the key issues and key challenges related to sustainable usage of space and how satellites can help to solve global societal sustainability problems (e.g., with remotely observing ice coverage and deforestation, allowing better communication, geonavigation). One of the key topics is quickly increasing space debris and how to prevent and remove it. At the same time the student will acquire knowledge on related topics such as satellite technology, manned space flights, space storms, Earth’s magnetosphere and ionosphere, aurora and solar activity. The course also handles several interdisciplinary related topics such as space law, -ethics and politics.

● The course is divided into Introduction and three themes. All themes have their own specific and concrete learning outcomes.

additional.en:
Completion methods

The course is completed by performing a multiple choice exam at the end of the course

Assessment practices and criteria

This is a MOOC course a student can take anytime. The evaluation is therefore a multiple choice questionnaire. The questions are formulated so that they are in line with general course learning objectives and theme wise learning objectives.

Activities and methods in support of learning

The course includes text, assignments, video interviews, and infographics.

Target groups

The course is intended for all interested in space. It suits well to BSc level studies for all faculties.

The course is offered at open university. 

Teaching period when the course will be offered

This is a MOOC course and can be taken any time.

Recommended time or stage of studies for completion

This course can be taken at any time during the studies

Language of instruction

English

This course is for students that are not studying business - Students at the School of Business can't participate. Information about the course is updated and published on the course platform at www.lito.fi. LITO courses are organised in co-operation with multiple universities. To enable registering credits when the course is completed, it is necessary to transfer data about the student from his/her home university to the university that is responsible for organizing the course. The data to be transferred consists of: name, gender, nationality, e-mail address, personal identification number and the home university. Data that is classified as secret is not transferred. Without a data transfer it is not possible to have the course credits registered.

No late registrations are accepted.

Please note that the course is organised on a separate platform, DigiCampus. Instructions for enrolment will be sent by email to registered students.

Ilmoittautuminen:

Opintojaksoa koskevat tiedot päivitetään www.lito.fi-sivustolle. Kurssi on tarkoitettu ainoastaan muille kuin kauppatieteiden opiskelijoille - Kauppakorkeakoulun opiskelijat eivät voi osallistua tälle kurssille. LITO-opintokokonaisuudessa opintojaksot järjestetään yliopistojen välisenä yhteistyönä. Jotta opiskelijan opintosuoritus saadaan kirjattua, hänestä siirretään kotiyliopiston rekisteristä opetusta järjestävän yliopiston rekisteriin seuraavat tiedot: nimi, sukupuoli, sähköpostiosoite, kansalaisuus, henkilötunnus ja kotiyliopisto. outcomes.fi:
Kurssin suorittanut opiskelija ymmärtää markkinatalouteen perustuvan
talousjärjestelmän tärkeimmät piirteet. Hän tunnistaa taloushistorian
suurimmat linjat, ja osaa arvioida instituutioiden merkitystä talouden
kehittymiselle. Erityisesti opiskelija hahmottaa hintamekanismin
merkityksen talouden voimavarojen kohdistamisessa, julkisen vallan
toimet markkinoita valvovana ja niiden puutteita korjaavana toimijana.
Hän tuntee sijoittamisen ja rahoitusmarkkinoiden merkityksen talouden
ja yritysten toiminnalle. Hän ymmärtää talouskasvuun ja
suhdannevaihteluun vaikuttavat tekijät ja osaa käyttää hankkimaansa
tietoa yhteiskunnallisten haasteiden jäsentämiseen. Opiskelija oppii
hankkimaan ja ymmärtämään kurssin ulkopuolista tilastomateriaalia..

content.fi:
Verkkokurssi muodostuu seitsemästä luvusta:
1. Talouden maailma - eli mikä saa maailman
pyörimään?
2. Markkinat ja hinnanmuodostus - eli mikä maksaa? ·
3. Ulkoisvaikutukset ja julkistalous - eli kuka tätä
laivaa ohjaa?
4. Rahoitusmarkkinat ja investoiminen - eli mistä rahat
kaikkeen löytyy?
5. Talouskasvu - eli miten tänne päästiin?
6. Suhdannevaihtelut - eli tuleeko kaikki, mikä menee
ylös myös alas?
7. Globaalit haasteet - eli voidaanko jatkaa tällä tiellä?

Completion methods

The student writes his or her thesis independently and submits the final thesis for grading. The thesis work is primarily supervised by the teacher whose Thesis Proposal Seminar the student has attended. The form of supervision is decided by each supervisor with the students.

Assessment practices and criteria

The learning outcomes set for master’s theses are described in the curriculum of the relevant degree programme, which is approved by the Faculty Council. Master’s theses are graded on the following scale: 5 = Excellent, 4 = Very Good, 3 = Good, 2 = Satisfactory, 1 = Passable, 0 = Fail.

Target groups

Master’s Programme in Economics

Annually in the spring term

The second spring term after completing all other advanced studies in economics

Study modules

ECOM-G300, ECOM-R300, ECOM-Y300

Language of learning

The thesis can be written in English, Finnish or Swedish.

outcomes.en: After completing the course, students will understand the factors underlying economic growth and how it manifests in developed and developing countries. Students will also gain an understanding of how economic growth can be empirically measured and compared between individual countries.
outcomes.fi: Opintojakson suorittamisen jälkeen opiskelija ymmärtää, mihin talouskasvu perustuu ja miten se ilmenee kehittyneissä ja kehittyvissä maissa. Opiskelijalle syntyy myös käsitys siitä, miten talouskasvua voidaan empiirisesti mitata ja verrata sitä eri maiden välillä.

prerequisites.en: TA1 Basics of Economics
prerequisites.fi: TA1 Taloustieteen perusteet

content.en: The following themes will be discussed on the course: methods of determining and measuring economic growth; the development of physical and human capital; economic adaptation to population growth as well as increases in productivity and educational level; the effect of the openness of the economy on growth; the causes underlying developmental differences between countries and empirical applications; the correlation between economic growth and income inequality; and the effect of the government on economic growth.
content.fi: Opintojaksolla käsitellään seuraavia aiheita: talouskasvun määritteleminen ja mittaus, fyysisen ja inhimillisen pääoman kertyminen, talouden sopeutuminen väestön, tuottavuuden ja koulutustason kasvuun, talouden avoimuuden vaikutus kasvuun, maiden välisten kehityserojen syyt ja empiiriset sovellukset, talouskasvun ja tuloerojen välinen riippuvuus sekä valtion vaikutus talouskasvuun.

outcomes.en: After completing the seminar, students will be able to apply scientific thinking and have the ability to analyse problems associated with economics. They will learn to write texts on economics, give presentations and contribute to discussion in a critical and constructive manner. The course also involves the assessment of other students’ written work, with the goal of teaching students to read texts on economics critically and conduct academic discussion on them. Another key goal of the peer assessment is to help students identify the weak points of their texts and, with the help of feedback, improve their output.
outcomes.fi: Opintojakson suoritettuaan opiskelija osaa soveltaa tieteellistä ajattelua ja hänellä on kyky käsitellä taloustieteellisiä ongelmia. Hän oppii kirjoittamaan taloustieteellistä tekstiä, esitelmöimään ja keskustelemaan kriittisesti mutta rakentavasti. Opintojaksolla arvioidaan myös toisten opiskelijoiden kirjoituksia. Arvioinnin tarkoitus on opettaa opiskelijaa lukemaan taloustieteellisiä tekstejä kriittisesti sekä käymään niistä tieteellistä keskustelua. Arvioinnin toinen tärkeä tarkoitus on auttaa kirjoittajaa näkemään tekstinsä heikot kohdat ja kommenttien myötä parantamaan työtään.

outcomes.en: To develop understanding of concepts and theoretical frameworks that describe, explain and prescribe the design and operation of production systems from strategy to daily operations. Operations management is perceived to cover both intra- and inter-organizational aspects in a global context. Besides providing relevant operations management concepts and theories, the objective is to learn to apply practical application of this knowledge through case studies and other assignments.
outcomes.fi: Ymmärtää tuotantojärjestelmien suunnittelua ja toimintaa kuvaava käsitteistö ja viitekehykset sekä strategisella että operatiivisella tasolla. Käsittää operaatioiden johtaminen sekä organisaation sisäisenä että organisaatioiden välisenä toimintana globaalilla tasolla. Tavoitteena on käsitteistön ja teorian hallinnan lisäksi soveltaa opittua käytäntöön harjoitustyössä.
outcomes.sv: Att förstå planering av produktionssystemen och begreppen beskrivande verksamhet samt referensramarna både på en strategisk och operativ nivå. Uppfatta ledning av operationer som både en intern verksamhet och en verksamhet mellan organisationer på en global nivå. Målet är utöver behärskning av begreppen och teorin att genom övningsarbeten lära sig tillämpa de inlärda kunskaperna i praktiken.

content.sv: Operationsstrategi, serviceoperationer, planering och utveckling av processer, val av processtyp och layout-planering, behärskning av kapacitet och materialflöden, globala verksamheter, logistik och behärskning av leveranskedjan, kvalitetsledning.

content.en:
The course covers key operations topics from demand analysis to operations strategy. Moving from demand analytics and forecasting models, to planning processes and coordination of supply and demand through sales and operations planning. Based on the analysis of the demand side, we will design competitive operations with the use of process analysis and design, factory physics and supply chain design. We will evaluate solutions to operations problems using the fundamental models and relevant analytics and simulation tools, valuing operations flexibility, costs, network design, and optimizing capacity and decisions under uncertainty. We will also cover state-of-the art of planning and control of supply chains from practice and theory.

Key focus area and viewpoint of the couse are sustainable operations and sustainability of the decisions by the operations managers. We will evaluate the options for local production and innovation for more resilient and sustainable operations that can be competitive and contribute to more sustainable businesses for future.

content.en:
The course is built around a number of real-life innovative solutions in operations and services. These solutions are presented by invited guest lecturers from industry and research groups. The students are this way - in class - taken to the cutting-edge of practice by the guest lecturer and challenged to address a current innovation problem. In doing so, the students will propose a real-life innovative solution.
Students will in groups work on one specific innovation problem, and evaluate solution proposals to all others presented in the course. Both solution and evaluation activities are conducted in a group. In class, innovation management theory is introduced and discussed in the context of the innovation problems and solution proposals.
An individual concluding assignment allow students to synthesize and reflect on the full course work.

outcomes.en:
After completing the course, you will be able to answer the following: 

  • What is an operating system (OS), what are its components and how does it work? What is a computer’s architecture and why is an OS needed? 
  • What is an OS process? How are processes executed, and how is the execution reflected in the states of the process? What is the difference between a process and a thread? 
  • How are processes working together in the OS? How is the OS scheduling the execution of the processes? 
  • How do processes communicate and synchronize their activity?  What is a deadlock? What is a livelock? What are semaphores and mutexes? 
  • What is the memory of the computer? How is the memory organized and how is it managed by the OS using pages and frames? 
  • What is the OS shell? How can the shell be used for automating tasks using scripts?  
  • What is Linux? How does Linux work? How can new functionality be added to the operating system? 
  • What are more specialized operating systems (e.g. embedded, fault-tolerant, for a quantum computer)? 
  • What are virtualization, a virtual container and an emulator? 

You will describe the typical data structures and algorithms commonly used in operating systems. You will gain the experience and confidence of using the shell (command line) for daily tasks. At the same time, you will learn the basics of (multi-threaded) system programming.

outcomes.en:
Upon completing the bachelor’s thesis, the student is able to

1. investigate a scientific or engineering topic in their area of interest and report the results of the investigation in written thesis form and in an oral presentation;

2. express the goals of the investigation as well-defined scientific or technical questions;

3. work systematically from an initially modest knowledge of the topic area toward an in-depth understanding;

4. find scientific literature relevant to the topic, read it analytically and critically, and identify its contributions and significance to their own work;

5. organise and analyse information from the literature, producing a clearly scoped, carefully argued, and well-presented synthesis and conclusions, answering the posed questions;

6. attribute information to its source following good scientific practices;

7. work independently and systematically, take expert advice, and participate constructively in a peer group;

8. abide by the standards of academic integrity and research ethics.
outcomes.fi:
Kandidaatintyön kirjoitettuaan opiskelija osaa

1. tutkia tieteellistä tai teknistä aihetta oman mielenkiintonsa alueelta ja raportoida tutkimuksen tulokset kirjallisen opinnäytteen muodossa sekä suullisessa esityksessä;

2. ilmaista tutkimuksen tavoitteet hyvin määriteltyinä tieteellisinä tai teknisinä kysymyksinä;

3. edetä järjestelmällisesti aihepiirin vähäisestä tuntemuksesta kohti sen syvällistä ymmärtämistä;

4. löytää aiheeseen liittyvää tutkimuskirjallisuutta, lukea sitä analyyttisesti ja kriittisesti sekä tunnistaa sen kontribuutiot ja merkityksen oman työnsä kannalta;

5. organisoida ja analysoida kirjallisuuden tietoa selkeästi rajatuksi, huolellisesti argumentoiduksi ja hyvin esitetyksi synteesiksi ja johtopäätöksiksi, jotka vastaavat asetettuihin kysymyksiin;

6. viitata tiedon lähteisiin noudattaen tieteellisen kirjoittamisen käytäntöjä;

7. työskennellä itsenäisesti ja järjestelmällisesti, ottaa vastaan asiantuntijan ohjausta, ja työskennellä rakentavasti vertaisryhmässä;

8. noudattaa akateemisen yhteisön eettisiä sääntöjä.
outcomes.sv:
Efter att ha slutfört kandidatarbetet kan studeranden

1. undersöka ett vetenskapligt eller tekniskt ämne inom sitt intresseområde och redovisa resultatet av undersökningen i form av ett skriftligt examensarbete och en muntlig presentation;

2. uttrycka undersökningens mål som väldefinierade vetenskapliga eller tekniska frågor;

3. arbeta systematiskt från en begränsad kunskap om ämnesområdet mot en fördjupad förståelse;

4. hitta vetenskaplig litteratur som är relevant för ämnet, läsa den analytiskt och kritiskt och identifiera dess bidrag och dess betydelse för sitt eget arbete;

5. organisera och analysera information från litteraturen, producera en tydligt avgränsad, noggrant argumenterad och väl presenterad syntes och slutsatser, och därmed svara på de ställda frågorna;

6. hänvisa till informationskällor enligt god vetenskaplig praxis;

7. arbeta självständigt och systematiskt, ta emot handledning av en expert och delta konstruktivt i en grupp av likar;

8. följa normerna för akademisk integritet och forskningsetik.

The key content of the course includes the history of social psychology, encompassing classical experimental studies that analyze the social cognition within social psychology. On the other hand, a central and more constructionist theoretical foundation is covered, including symbolic interactionism, social representations, and the theory of cultural-historical activity.

Additionally, during the course, participants will learn about the application of social psychology to technological development.

content.en: In Digital Ethics and Sustainability course we explore key challenges facing the environment, society, business and the Information technology sector, and ask some difficult and justified questions about how to address these challenges. outcomes.en:
The purpose of the course is to give an overview and introduction to the ICT ecosystem and how it tackles, or harms, a sustainable future. All technologies have a handprint (the positive effects) and a footprint (negative effects). As the world is working towards a more sustainable future, ICT is at the heart of the development, and provides many positive solutions (handprint.) Yet, at the same time, ICT consumes increasing amounts of energy and natural resources, and causes a major footprint on the world as a whole.
The goal of the course is to raise awareness of the impact of ICT and in particular the hidden footprint.

content.en:
Big data is transforming the way we do business, socialize, conduct research, and govern society. Tools like AI and advanced analytics offer tremendous potential to enhance our lives, enabling new services and products. These technologies provide organizations with extended capabilities to lessen their environmental and social impacts, fostering innovative and responsible solutions. However, they can also introduce new environmental and social challenges. There are growing concerns about the negative externalities of data analytics, such as their roles in privacy invasion, inequality, behavior manipulation, opacity, and other related harms.

This course is designed to complement the focus of most data analytics courses, which typically center on what can be done with data and AI. Instead, we will explore what should and should not be done. Our goal is to encourage the practice of responsible data science, considering the impacts of various analytics tools and methods on individuals, population groups, and society at large. We will cover topics including ethics, legal compliance, data quality, algorithmic fairness and diversity, transparency of data and algorithms, privacy, and data protection. Additionally, we will engage in discussions and debates about how society can mitigate the negative externalities posed by big data, advanced analytics, and AI. These conversations will draw on examples from various fields such as technology, retail, marketing, healthcare, finance, and other public institutions.

Designed for broad accessibility, this course emphasizes the societal role of big data, advanced analytics, and AI, rather than hands-on analytics skills. While some familiarity with data analytics or quantitative methods is beneficial, our focus is on fostering a holistic understanding of these transformative technologies and their ethical dimensions.

outcomes.en:
After successfully completing this course students will

  • Be familiar with concepts of infinite sequences and series
  • Understand the principles of how a sum of infinite series is formed
  • Recognize different types of series
  • Understand what is meant by convergence and divergence of a sequence and series
  • Master various tests for convergence of series and discern situations in which to apply them
  • Represent elementary functions, such as trigonometric functions and logarithms, as series, find domains in which these series converge, and use these series representations to approximate values of functions
outcomes.fi: Opiskelija tuntee sarjan suppenemisen määritelmän ja osaa sen perusteella tutkia sarjan suppenemista. Hän tietää geometrisen ja harmonisen sarjan sekä p-sarjojen yleiset ominaisuudet. Opiskelija osaa tutkia sarjojen suppenemista suppenemistestien avulla. Hän tuntee vuorottelevien ja manipuloitujen sarjojen sekä itseisesti ja ehdollisesti suppenevien sarjojen ominaisuuksia. Opiskelija tuntee potenssisarjat ja osaa määrittää niiden suppenemisvälin. Hän ymmärtää sarjan tasaisen suppenemisen merkityksen, kun tutkitaan summafunktion jatkuvuutta, derivoituvuutta ja integroituvuutta. Lisäksi hän osaa approksimoida funktioita Taylorin polynomeilla ja pystyy arvioimaan approksimoinnissa syntyvän virheen suuruutta. Opiskelija tietää, mitä ovat Taylorin sarjat.

prerequisites.en:
Either the collection of the three Calculus courses

  • MAT11006: Calculus 1A: Limits and Differentiation
  • MAT11007: Calculus 1B: Integration
  • MAT11008: Advanced Calculus

or the collection of the three Finnish analysis courses

  • MAT11003: Raja-arvot
  • MAT11004: Differentiaalilaskenta
  • MAT11005: Integraalilaskenta

Students need to be fluent with finding limits, derivatives and integrals as well as proving results based on definitions, especially producing epsilon and delta type proofs.
prerequisites.fi: Opintojaksot MAT11003 Raja-arvot, MAT11004 Differentiaalilaskenta ja MAT11005 Integraalilaskenta.

content.en:
Course covers the following main topics

  1. Sequences and Series
  2. Convergence
  3. Geometric Series, p-series
  4. Alternating Series
  5. Convergence Tests: Integral, Comparison, Ratio, Root, Absolute Convergence
  6. Power Series, Abel’s Theorem, Radius of Convergence
  7. Uniform convergence, Differentiating and Integrating Series
  8. Maclaurin and Taylor Polynomials and Series, Approximating Functions

additional.en:
Target group

NB: This page concerns online course held in English, to see information about the Finnish lecture based equivalent course, please change language to Finnish.

Course is part of bachelor degree program in mathematical sciences and therein intermediate studies.


Timing

This online course takes place in period IV.


Completion methods

This is an online course. All course material and activities can be found on the online course area. There is a final proctored paper and pencil exam at the end of the course.


Activities and teaching methods in support of learning

Studying in this course follows a weekly cycle. Each week students are expected to:

  1. Watch the prerecorded lectures or read the text allocated for the next workshop at the class Moodle site.
  2. Solve quiz problems. They will help to prepare for the workshops.
  3. Submit solutions to workshop problems by Wednesday evening.
  4. Grade and give feedback to other students’ workshop submissions by Sunday evening.
  5. Also ask questions, hints for solving problems etc. in the discussion forum.

Assessment practices and criteria

Continuous formative assessment takes place throughout the course by weekly quizzes and workshops. These will give homework extra credit maximum of 5 points.

Final paper and pencil exam with maximum of 30 points will measure comprehensively the learning goals.

Scale 1-5 of grades will be used. Passing course with grade 1 will require approximately half of the points of the exam and for the best grade approximately 5/6 of the exam points are required. Homework extra credit points will be added to the exam points.


Responsible person

Matti Pauna

name.sv: 5G Technologies and Services for Business and Entrepreneurs

outcomes.en:
At the end of the course, a successful student will be able to:

• Recognize the key technological components of 5G, with emphasis on radio access & core network part of its architecture.

• Define and explain the basic concepts and terms used for analysis of entrepreneurship and entrepreneurial finance.

• Identify new entrepreneurial business ideas enabled by 5G technologies, iteratively improving them by soliciting feedback and evaluating their market viability.

• Consider customer and user-centered development of emerging services with 5G technology.

• Know how to plan, prepare, execute, document, and evaluate agile pilot testing based on new entrepreneurial business ideas enabled by 5G.

content.en:
The content of this course is divided into four different units, whose contents are expanded as follows:

• Unit 1: 5G mobile technologies. From 1G to 5G. Mobile (4G/LTE & 5G/NR) vs. Wireless (Wi[1]Fi) radio access technologies. Mobile network architecture. 5G standardization. 5G technology enablers. Machine-type communications and Narrow-Band IoT. Non-terrestrial networks (space and aerial).

• Unit 2: Human-centred design, prototyping and piloting. Human-centred design, prototyping and piloting of 5G products and mobile services. Exploration and analysis of user needs and customer requirements for specifying and prioritising product features and service characteristics. Elaboration on the development of prototypes for real-life evaluation and piloting with anticipated users and customers in living lab surroundings.

• Unit 3: Introduction to entrepreneurship. Introduction to entrepreneurship. Role of 5G in the development of Sub-Saharan Africa (Education, business, agriculture, etc.). Digitalized vs Conventional Entrepreneurship. Connections between Globalization, International Competition, International Trade & Development cooperation, and Entrepreneurial Ideas that 5G can unlock in Global South.

• Unit 4: Business models, commercialization, finance. Business models, commercialization, finance. Entrepreneurial Ideas from Global South. Tactics for different types of Pitches. Business Model Canvas (including Business Finance). Sources of financing Entrepreneurial Ventures (long-term financing, capital structure, common stock, different types of debt). Bankability & financing for Start-ups (definition, risks).

name.fi: Digital Technologies and Services for Rural Communities

outcomes.en:
After approving this course, the students should be able to:

· Know the fundamentals of wireless communications, including the modeling of the radio channels and the analog frontend blocks (antennas, amplifiers, etc.)

· Understand the processing that is carried out in the Physical and Data Link layers of a wireless communication system, and its relevant Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).

· Know the main differences between wide area (long-range/satellite & mobile) and local area (short-range/WiFi & LoRa) radiocommunication technologies.

· Skill how to plan the deployment of a (private) wireless communication system (Wi-Fi, SatCom, LoRa) and carry out some practical measurements.

· Know the different renewable sources of energy to power a low-power connectivity node and dimension the size of solar panel for proper operation.

Identify new entrepreneurial business ideas, enabled by wireless connectivity technologies in rural areas, considering customer and user-centered development of digital services.

· Skill how to plan the deployment of a (private) wireless communication system (Wi-Fi, SatCom, LoRa) and carry out some practical measurements.

· Know the different renewable sources of energy to power a low-power connectivity node and dimension the size of solar panel for proper operation.

Identify new entrepreneurial business ideas, enabled by wireless connectivity technologies in rural areas, considering customer and user-centered development of digital services.

content.en:
The content of this course is divided into four different units, whose contents are expanded as follows:

· Unit 1: Wireless communications. Introduction to wireless communications, fundamentals of mobile communications, hardware and wireless link budgets, modulation and error control coding, multi-antenna systems (MIMO), mobile communications systems (4G & 5G), wireless communication systems (WPAN/Bluetooth, WLAN/WiFi & LPWAN/LoRa), Key Performance Indictors (Energy and Spectral efficiency).

· Unit 2: Data networks. Introduction to data networks, architectures of data networks, routing in data networks. Introduction to satellite communication networks.

· Unit 3: Sustainable energy sources. Renewable energy sources, technologies for renewable energy systems, dimensioning renewable energy generation systems, energy storage devices. Practices and new habits to maximize energy efficiency.

· Unit 4: Human and social aspects of digital technologies. User-centered mobile service design, design with participation from rural communities, social aspects of community networks.

content.en:
The introduction of cloud computing and the explosive growth of mobile computing and new online services have brought new ways of structuring computing systems: microservice architectures and serverless computing.

This course is targeted at students with at least a basic understanding of service architectures and scalable architectures, and builds on top of that to look at what possibilities and new challenges microservice architectures and serverless computing brings on top of “classic” service architectures.

This course is about microservice and serverless system design, not implementation. This course will not teach how to program or deploy microservices. It will, however, cover multiservice system design and design of scalable and fault-tolerant services.

Course contents

  • Introduction
  • Microservice ecosystem
  • System design
  • Failures
  • Service architectures
  • Configuration and discovery
  • Scalability
  • Deployment
  • Service evolution
  • Serverless

outcomes.en: After passing the course the students can analyse and forecast time series using regression models and ARIMA-models. Students are able to apply linear regression model to analyse and forecast dependent variable under the model assumptions. In addition, the students are able to conduct diagnostic tests to validate the model assumptions. Students are familiar with the concept weakly stationary processes and they understand the most important related concepts including the autocorrelation function, and partial autocorrelation function. Students are also able to apply these functions in analysing real time series, for example, in recognising seasonal fluctuations. After taking the course, the students know ARIMA-models and their key properties. In addition, the students are able to model and predict the future behaviour of observed time series using ARIMA-models. The students also know basic concepts of dynamic regression models.

outcomes.en:
After successfully completing this course students will

  • Be familiar with concepts of infinite sequences and series
  • Understand the principles of how a sum of infinite series is formed
  • Recognize different types of series
  • Understand what is meant by convergence and divergence of a sequence and series
  • Master various tests for convergence of series and discern situations in which to apply them
  • Represent elementary functions, such as trigonometric functions and logarithms, as series, find domains in which these series converge, and use these series representations to approximate values of functions
  • Understand concept of uniform convergence, determine whether a series converges uniformly, and use it to differentiate and integrate a series term by term

prerequisites.en:
Calculus IA: Limits and Differentiation
Calculus IB: Integration
Advanced Calculus

content.en:
Course covers the following main topics

  1. Sequences and Series
  2. Convergence
  3. Geometric Series, p-series
  4. Alternating Series
  5. Convergence Tests: Integral, Comparison, Ratio, Root, Absolute Convergence
  6. Power Series, Abel’s Theorem, Radius of Convergence
  7. Uniform convergence, Differentiating and Integrating Series
  8. Maclaurin and Taylor Polynomials and Series, Approximating Functions
  9. Specifc topics to programme's needs, such as Fourier transform

additional.en:
Completion methods

This is an online course. All course material and activities can be found on the online course area. There is a final proctored paper and pencil exam at the end of the course.

Assessment practices and criteria

Continuous formative assessment takes place throughout the course by weekly quizzes and workshops. These will give homework extra credit maximum of 5 points or the course can be completed based on homework.

Course can also be passed by taking an exam.

Scale 1-5 of grades will be used. Passing course with grade 1 will require approximately half of the points of the exam and for the best grade approximately 5/6 of the exam points are required. Homework extra credit points will be added to the exam points.

Activities and methods in support of learning

Studying in this course follows a weekly cycle. Each week students are expected to:

  1. Watch the prerecorded lectures or read the text allocated for the next workshop at the class Moodle site.
  2. Submit solutions to workshop tasks by Wednesday evening. Late submissions will not be accepted.
  3. Grade and give feedback to other students’ workshop submissions by Sunday evening.
  4. Also ask questions, hints for solving problems etc. in the discussion forum.
Target groups

Programme: Bachelor's programme in Science. (the course is taught by Matemaattisten tieteiden kandiohjelma)

Module: Basics studies in Mathematics.

The course is optional within the programme but compulsory for the mathematics study track.

The course is available to the students of other programmes upon agreement with the teacher.

Teaching period when the course will be offered

The course is offered in the spring every year in Period 4.

Recommended time or stage of studies for completion

Within mathematics study track, first year of studies.

In other study tracks, according to schedule of track/programme

Study module

Intermediate Studies in Mathematics and Statistics.

Language of instruction

English

learningMaterial.en:
All necessary study material can be found in the course area. Most topics are covered in videos created by prof. Mika Seppälä. Some topics are covered in the book "Introduction to Real Analysis" by Trench, available in the course area.

Standard Calculus text books, such as Adams' or Stewart's Calculus books can be used as side material among others.
The parts covering Series in the Finnish “Analyysia reaaliluvuilla” (Harjulehto, Klén, Koskenoja) can be recommended for Finnish speaking students (though language of communication is always English).
NB: sequence of covering topics in these books may vary from that in the course.

Opintojakso kuuluu pakollisena opintona kokonaisuuteen MAT210 Matematiikan aineopinnot ja valinnaisena kokonaisuuksiin MFK-M200 Matematiikka, aineopinnot, aineenopettajakoulutus sekä MFK-M300 Matematiikka, syventävät opinnot, aineenopettajakoulutus. Ajoitus

Opintojaksoa suositellaan opintokokonaisuuden MAT210 suorittajille suoritettavaksi toisena opiskeluvuotena.


Toteutus

Opintojakso koostuu viikottaisista luennoista ja laskuharjoituksista sekä itsenäisestä työskentelystä.


Oppimista tukevat aktiviteetit ja opetusmenetelmät

Luento-opetuksen tukena on viikoittaiset luennot ja harjoitustehtävät. Luento-opetukseen osallistuvia kannustetaan tehtävien ratkaisemiseen ryhmissä esimerkiksi Exactumin 3. kerroksen yhteistyötilassa Ratkomossa.


Arviointimenetelmät ja -kriteerit

Luento-opetukseen osallistuttaessa suoritus määräytyy kurssikokeesta ja harjoitustehtävistä ennen opetuksen alkua kurssisivulla ilmoittettavalla tavalla. Luento-opetuksen aikana kerätyistä harjoitustehtävä pisteistä on saa lisäpisteitä yleistenttiin luento-opetuksen kurssisivulla ilmoitettavalla tavalla.

Opintojakso koostuu viikottaisista luennoista ja laskuharjoituksista sekä itsenäisestä työskentelystä.


Oppimista tukevat aktiviteetit ja opetusmenetelmät

Luento-opetuksen tukena on viikoittaiset luennot ja harjoitustehtävät. Luento-opetukseen osallistuvia kannustetaan tehtävien ratkaisemiseen ryhmissä esimerkiksi Exactumin 3. kerroksen yhteistyötilassa Ratkomossa.


Arviointimenetelmät ja -kriteerit

Luento-opetukseen osallistuttaessa suoritus määräytyy kurssikokeesta ja harjoitustehtävistä ennen opetuksen alkua kurssisivulla ilmoittettavalla tavalla. Luento-opetuksen aikana kerätyistä harjoitustehtävä pisteistä on saa lisäpisteitä yleistenttiin luento-opetuksen kurssisivulla ilmoitettavalla tavalla.

outcomes.en: The course gives a working knowledge in general topology, also called point-set topology. The material is fundamental in a wide-range of further studies in mathematics, especially in analysis and geometry. During the course the student becomes familiar with the fundamentals of general topology, such as topological spaces and bases, connectedness, compactness, separation and countability axioms, metrization and extension theorems. The student learns how to prove basic properties of these concepts, connections between the concepts as well as how to apply them.

prerequisites.en: Bachelor studies, including Topology I

content.en:
Fundamentals of general topology, including: topological spaces and 
bases, connectedness, compactness, separation and countability axioms, 
metrization and extension theorems.

outcomes.en:
The goal of the course is to design an implementable business experiment in product management that helps a partner organization to develop either its offering or the capabilities towards exploring these opportunities later. The project is based on a self-identified topic and a related customer and user need that serves as a basis for sustainable value creation for society and business. The final outcomes of the project depend on what the topic, needs, and the related opportunities.

After the course, the students will understand the early stages of the entrepreneurial process and principles of product management. More specifically, the student:

  • Recognizes the phases and elements of the entrepreneurial process of identifying and developing opportunities, and can relate these to the elements of effectuation theory
  • Develop and justify the value and purposefulness of a solution from the perspectives of business and society
  • Recognizes the key elements and characteristics of business and organization development, and can work with partners and stakeholders in order to create and develop opportunities
  • Is able to apply research methods to acquire data on customer preferences and interpret the results
  • Recognizes the elements of a business model, is able to use business model tools to analyze existing businesses, and has preliminary skills to analytically compare businesses and identify the crucial aspects of the (business?) development process.
  • Recognizes his/her own reactions to an ambiguous search process
  • Can direct and develop the working methods of a project group with discussion and facilitation tools
outcomes.fi:
Kurssin tavoitteena on luoda kestävää arvoa laatimalla itse määritettyyn tarpeeseen liittyvä, kokeiluille perustuva ja kumppanille soveltuva etenemissuunnitelma uuden tai nykyisen tuotteen kehittämiseksi. Soveltuvissa tapauksissa tämä saattaa myös projektin aikana tarkentua muihin tuotteeseen liittyviin kokeiluihin ja kehittämiseen.  

Projektin pohjana on itse tunnistettu käyttäjien ja asiakkaiden tarve. Tämä tarve valitaan lähtökohtaisesti siten, että projektissa on mahdollista luoda sekä kestävää yhteiskunnallista että liiketoiminnallista arvoa kehittämällä yrityksen tai organisaation tuotetta tai tarjoamaa. Projektia ohjaa aiheen vaatima tarkoituksenmukaisuus ja toteutettavuus, joten lopulliset tulokset riippuvat kustakin aiheesta, kumppanista ja projektista.

Kurssin suoritettuaan, opiskelijalla on käsitys yrittäjyyden ensimmäisistä vaiheista sekä tuotejohtamisen perusteista. Opiskelija osaa

  • tunnistaa yrittäjyys- ja kehitysprojektien tyypillisiä alkuvaiheita
  • kehittää ja perustella tunnistetun tarpeen merkitystä ja arvoa käyttäjän, liiketoiminnan sekä yhteiskunnan näkökulmista
  • tunnistaa organisaatioiden kehitystoimintojen pääpiirteitä ja työskennellä kehittävällä ja mahdollisuuksia kehkeyttävällä tavalla kumppaneiden ja muiden sidosryhmien kanssa
  • hyödyntää yhtä tai useampaa tutkimusmenetelmää käyttäjän ja/tai asiakkaan tarpeiden kartoittamiseksi sekä kehitettävän ratkaisun validoinniksi
  • tunnistaa yritysten liiketoimintamallien keskeisimpiä piirteitä, ja vertailla ja analysoida eri yritysten sekä nykyisiä että mahdollisia liiketoimintamalleja
  • luoda perusteltu, koeteltu, ja kumppanille soveltuva suunnitelma tuotteen kehittämiseksi 
  • tunnistaa ja eritellä omaa toimintaansa ja reaktioitaan avoimessa ja määrittelemättömässä ongelmanratkaisuprosessissa
  • suunnata ja kehittää projektiryhmän työskentelyä keskusteluiden ja fasilitoivien työkalujen avulla
outcomes.sv:
Målet med kursen är att utforma ett genomförbart experiment on produktledning som hjälper en partnerorganisation att utveckla antingen sitt erbjudande eller förmågan att utforska dessa möjligheter senare. Projektet bygger på ett av studenten identifierat ämne och till detta relaterat användar- och kundbehov, som fungerar som grund för hållbart värdeskapande för samhället och näringslivet. Projektet styrs av ämnets relevans och genomförbarhet, så de slutliga resultaten kommer att bero på varje ämne, partner och projekt.

Efter avslutad kurs har studenten en uppfattning om de första etapperna av entreprenörskap och om pricipen i produktledning. Studenten kan

  • identifiera typiska faser och element i entreprenörskaps- och utvecklingsprojekt och analysera dem med hjälp av en resursorienterad utvecklingsprocess (effektuation)
  • utveckla och motivera lösningens betydelse och värde ur både socialt och affärsmässigt perspektiv
  • identifiera nyckelelementen och egenskaperna i affärs- och organisationsutveckling, och kan arbeta med partners och intressenter för att skapa och utveckla möjligheter
  • använda en eller flera forskningsmetoder för att kartlägga användarens och/eller kundens behov
  • identifiera viktiga funktioner i affärsmodeller och jämföra och analysera olika företags affärsmodeller, både befintliga och potentiella
  • identifiera och analysera sina egna handlingar och reaktioner i en öppen och ospecificerad problemlösningsprocess
  • kan styra och utveckla arbetsmetoderna för en projektgrupp med diskussions- och faciliterings verktyg

content.en: The course consists of a self-directed group project that consists of  two parts. The first part is based on an entrepreneurial search process, where you will independently and proactively search for an initial definition of a user need, and then explore opportunities to partner with an appropriate and willing organization. The second part is based on working with the partner(s) to explore how it could explore a new opportunity to renew its offering.The project is supported by coaching, reflection and presentation meetings.
content.fi: Kurssi muodostuu ryhmässä tehtävästä, itseohjautuvasta projektista, jossa on kaksi keskeistä vaihetta. Ensimmäisessä vaiheessa identifioidaan kiinnostava ja lupaava aihe ja selvitetään konkreettisia ja merkityksellisiä tarpeita siihen liittyen. Näiden pohjalta etsitään yksi tai useampi kumppani ja määritetään yhteinen projekti. Toisessa vaiheessa kumppanin kanssa kehitetään mahdollisia keinoja vastata tarkennettuihin tarpeisiin, ja muotoillaan tulokset toteuttamiskelpoiseksi kokeiluksi. Projektin rinnalla kurssin yhteis- ja ohjaustapaamisissa suunnataan ja kirkastetaan projektin etenemistä.
content.sv: Kursen består av ett självstyrt grupp-projekt med två viktiga faser. Det första steget är att identifiera ett intressant och lovande ämne och sedan identifiera de konkreta och relevanta behoven för det. Baserat på detta arbete väljs en eller flera partners varefter ett gemensamt projekt kan definieras. Den andra fasen består av utvecklingsarbete med partnern, då utforskas nya möjligheter att möta de identifierade behoven. Resultaten kommer att utformas till ett genomförbart experiment. Projektet stöds av coaching, reflektion och handledningsmöten.

content.en: The cross-cutting theme of the course is to give you methods for recognizing factors and developing skills affecting study wellbeing. These are focused on through weekly topics: foundations of study motivation; studies as part of life and recognizing meaningful values to oneself; time management skills and getting things done; emotions promoting and hindering study progress; strengths and stress management skills.
content.fi: Kurssin läpileikkaavana tarkoituksena on, että saat työkaluja omaan opiskeluhyvinvointiisi vaikuttavien osa-alueiden tunnistamiseen ja kehittämiseen. Näihin perehdyt viikoittaisten opiskelutaitoteemojen kautta, joita ovat opiskelumotivaation perusta, opiskelu osana elämänkulkua ja itselle merkityksellisten arvojen tunnistaminen, ajankäyttö ja taito saada aikaan, opiskelun etenemistä edistävät ja estävät tunteet, omat vahvuudet sekä stressinhallinta.
content.sv: Kursens genomgående grundidé är att ge dig verktyg för identifiering och utveckling av delområden som påverkar ditt studievälmående. Du bekantar dig med dessa verktyg via veckobaserat arbete med teman i studiekunskaper. Temana är grunden för studiemotivationen, studier som del av livet med identifiering av för dig betydelsefulla värden, tidsanvändning och kunskap att får saker gjorda, känslor som främjar och hindrar framgång av studier, dina styrkor, och stresshantering.

content.en:
Entrepreneurial mindset and entrepreneurial skills are beneficial and needed in all kinds of organizations. The aim of the course is not to help students to start their own business, but rather to equip them with entrepreneurial mindset, that they could use in any life situation. 

Entrepreneurial skills can be divided into three subgroups, ideas & opportunities, resources, and into action. Inside  these subgroups, there are many different skills and ways of thinking, that can be utilized in various operations. Some of these skills and ways of thinking are for example: collaboration with other professionals, seeking and identifying opportunities, and communication of results. 

The course focuses inspecting and practicing entrepreneurial skills and entrepreneurial mindset, and reflecting these in relation to their own future.
content.fi:
Yrittäjähenkinen ajattelu ja yrittäjyystaidot ovat hyödyllisiä ja tarpeen kaikenlaisissa organisaatioissa. Tämän kurssin tarkoituksena ei ole auttaa opiskelijoita perustamaan omaa yritystä, vaan valjastaa heidät yrittäjähenkisellä ajattelulla, jota he voivat hyödyntää missä vain elämäntilanteessa. 

Yrittäjyystaidot voidaan jakaa kolmeen osa-alueeseen ideoihin ja mahdollisuuksiin, resursseihin, sekä toiminnan aloittamiseen. Näiden sisällä on useita erilaisia taitoja sekä ajatusmalleja joita voi hyödyntää erilaisissa toimissa. Näitä ovat esimerkiksi: yhteistyö eri tahojen kanssa, mahdollisuuksien etsiminen ja tunnistaminen, sekä tulostenviestintä. 

Kurssilla tarkastellaan sekä harjoitellaan yrittäjyystaitoja sekä yrittäjähenkistä ajattelua ja reflektoidaan näitä suhteessa omaan tulevaisuuteen.
content.sv:
Entreprenörsanda och entreprenöriell kompetens är fördelaktigt och behövs i alla typer av organisationer. Målet med kursen är inte att hjälpa studerande att starta egna företag, utan snarare att utrusta dem med entreprenörsanda, som de kan använda i alla livssituationer. 

Entreprenöriell kompetens kan delas in i tre undergrupper: idéer och möjligheter, resurser och att skrida till handling. Inom dessa undergrupper finns många olika färdigheter och sätt att tänka, som kan användas i olika verksamheter. Exempel på sådana färdigheter och tänkesätt är: samarbete med andra yrkesverksamma, att söka och identifiera möjligheter, samt att kommunicera resultat. 

I kursen får den studerande undersöka och öva på entreprenöriell kompetens och entreprenörsanda samt reflektera över dessa i relation till sin egen framtid.
